items.body:
Dispatch-ready encoding debt for the SSI spousal-deeming benefit rule and the definitions that classify SSI couples. Companion PolicyEngine work: PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10138 (issue) and the pull request that cites this issue as `axiom: <this issue> queued`. Related: #1626, which queues 416.1202 and 416.1205 (resource deeming) and has the same corpus blocker. No handwritten RuleSpec has been created.

## Encoding debt and search evidence

PolicyEngine-US capped SSI under spousal income deeming at the individual Federal benefit rate, so a claimant with income of their own could get more with deeming than without it. 20 CFR 416.1163(e)(2) makes the benefit the lesser of the couple computation and the individual rate less the claimant's own countable income. PolicyEngine-US also found SSI couples (joint claims, and the ineligible spouse whose income is deemed) through tax-unit head and spouse roles, which do not appear in 416.1801(c), 416.1806 or 416.1160(d).

I listed the tracked tree of rulespec-us `origin/main` at `16a667719` (`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- us/statutes/42 us/regulations`). The SSI modules present are `us/statutes/42/1382/a/1-3`, `1382/b`, `1382/e/1`, `1382a/b/2`, `1382a/b/4`, `1382b/a`, `1382c/a/1-2`, `1382f/a` and `1382f/c`. None is under `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/`. `us/statutes/42/1382/b.yaml` encodes the statutory benefit with and without an eligible spouse and reads income as a supplied input. It has no deeming rule and does not say who is an eligible spouse. An issue search for 416.1163, spousal deeming and eligible spouse found only #1626 and LTSS issues (#1578, #1588-#1592), which concern Medicaid spousal impoverishment rather than SSI.

New modules and companion fixtures:

- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1163.yaml` and `1163.test.yaml`, corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1163`. Pinned corpus line 6 of `data/corpus/provisions/us/regulation/2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl`.
- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1801.yaml` and `1801.test.yaml`, corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1801` (line 12), for the eligible-spouse definition in 416.1801(c).
- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1806.yaml` and `1806.test.yaml`, corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1806` (line 14), for who is a spouse.
- The ineligible-spouse definition in 416.1160(d), corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1160` (line 4). Encode it as a rule in a `1160.yaml` module, or in `1163.yaml` with a 416.1160(d) proof excerpt.
- Import the Federal benefit rates from `us/statutes/42/1382/b` and `us/statutes/42/1382f/a`. Treat countable income after 416.1112 and 416.1124 and the 416.1163(b)-(c) allocations as exact, legally scoped leaf inputs until those sections are encoded. Do not substitute tax-unit roles or tax dependency for spouse or household relationships.

## Corpus and signed encoder blocker

The same blocker as #1626. The rulespec-us toolchain pins corpus release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap`, corpus ref `8f7d60aaced28ee4252b9237f9d6e02360dc34bc`. At that ref, `2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl` has rows for 416.1160, 416.1163, 416.1801, 416.1802 and 416.1806 (source format `ecfr-xml`, source as of 2026-07-14). The pinned release manifest `manifests/releases/us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap.json` does not include the `2026-07-23-title-20-part-416` scope, so these rows are not dispatchable from the pinned release. Generated content must come from the signed encoder with its protected signer, and the billed run needs its own approval (#1403, #1416). The `.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml` pins are axiom-encode `0.2.2092` (`3bf5a2af`), rules engine `89571cc2` and corpus `8f7d60aa`. Refresh and verify all refs at dispatch time.

## Regulation (verbatim, pinned corpus rows)

### 20 CFR 416.1163(d), (e) and (f)(5)

https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-K/section-416.1163

> (d) Determining your eligibility for SSI. (1) If the amount of your ineligible spouse's income that remains after appropriate allocations is not more than the difference between the Federal benefit rate for an eligible couple and the Federal benefit rate for an eligible individual, there is no income to deem to you from your spouse. In this situation, we subtract only your own countable income from the Federal benefit rate for an individual to determine whether you are eligible for SSI benefits.
>
> (2) If the amount of your ineligible spouse's income that remains after appropriate allocations is more than the difference between the Federal benefit rate for an eligible couple and the Federal benefit rate for an eligible individual, we treat you and your ineligible spouse as an eligible couple. We do this by:
>
> (i) Combining the remainder of your spouse's unearned income with your own unearned income and the remainder of your spouse's earned income with your earned income;
>
> (ii) Applying all appropriate income exclusions in §§ 416.1112 and 416.1124; and
>
> (iii) Subtracting the couple's countable income from the Federal benefit rate for an eligible couple. (See § 416.2025(b) for determination of the State supplementary payment amount.)
>
> (e) Determining your SSI benefit. (1) In determining your SSI benefit amount, we follow the procedure in paragraphs (a) through (d) of this section. However, we use your ineligible spouse's income in the second month prior to the current month. We vary this rule if any of the exceptions in § 416.1160(b)(2) applies (for example, if this is the first month you are eligible for payment of an SSI benefit or if you are again eligible after at least a month of being ineligible). In the first month of your eligibility for payment (or re-eligibility), we deem your ineligible spouse's income in the current month to determine both whether you are eligible for a benefit and the amount of your benefit. In the second month, we deem your ineligible spouse's income in that month to determine whether you are eligible for a benefit but we deem your ineligible spouse's income in the first month to determine the amount of your benefit.
>
> (2) Your SSI benefit under the deeming rules cannot be higher than it would be if deeming did not apply. Therefore, your benefit is the lesser of the amount computed under the rules in paragraph (d)(2) of this section or the amount remaining after we subtract only your own countable income from an individual's Federal benefit rate.
>
> (5) You become subject to the $30 Federal benefit rate. If you become a resident of a medical care facility and the $30 Federal benefit rate applies, we do not deem your ineligible spouse's income to you to determine your eligibility for SSI benefits beginning with the first month for which the $30 Federal benefit rate applies. In determining your benefit amount beginning with the first month for which the $30 Federal benefit rate applies, we use only your own countable income in a prior month, excluding any income deemed to you in that month from your ineligible spouse.

### 20 CFR 416.1163(g), Examples 2 and 3 (September 1986 rates: $336 individual, $504 couple)

> Example 2. In September 1986, Mr. Jones, a disabled individual, lives with his ineligible spouse, Mrs. Jones, and ineligible child, Christine. Mr. Jones and Christine have no income. Mrs. Jones has earned income of $401 a month and unearned income of $252 a month. Before we deem any income, we allocate $168 to Christine. We take the $168 allocation from Mrs. Jones' $252 unearned income, leaving $84 in unearned income. Since Mrs. Jones' total remaining income ($84 unearned plus $401 earned) is more than $168, which is the difference between the September Federal benefit rate for an eligible couple and the September Federal benefit rate for an eligible individual, we compute the combined countable income as we do for a couple. We apply the $20 general income exclusion to the unearned income, reducing it further to $64. We then apply the earned income exclusion ($65 plus one-half the remainder) to Mrs. Jones' earned income of $401, leaving $168. We combine the $64 countable unearned income and $168 countable earned income, and compare it ($232) with the $504 September Federal benefit rate for a couple, and determine that Mr. Jones is eligible. [...]
>
> Example 3. In September 1986, Mr. Smith, a disabled individual, lives with his ineligible spouse, Mrs. Smith, who earns $201 per month. Mr. Smith receives a pension (unearned income) of $100 a month. Since Mrs. Smith's income is greater than $168, [...] we deem all of her income to be available to both Mr. and Mrs. Smith and compute the combined countable income for the couple. We apply the $20 general income exclusion to Mr. Smith's $100 unearned income, leaving $80. Then we apply the earned income exclusion ($65 plus one-half of the remainder) to Mrs. Smith's $201, leaving $68. This gives the couple total countable income of $148. This is less than the $504 September Federal benefit rate for a couple, so Mr. Smith is eligible based on deeming. [...]

### 20 CFR 416.1801(c) (definitions)

https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-R/section-416.1801

> Eligible spouse means a person— (1) Who is eligible for SSI, (2) Whom we consider the spouse of another person who is eligible for SSI, and (3) Who was living in the same household with that person on— (i) The first day of the month following the date the application is filed (for the initial month of eligibility for payment based on that application); (ii) The date a request for reinstatement of eligibility is filed (for the month of such request); or (iii) The first day of the month, for all other months. An individual is considered to be living with an eligible spouse during temporary absences as defined in § 416.1149 and while receiving continued benefits under section 1611(e)(1) (E) or (G) of the Act.
>
> Spouse means a person's husband or wife under the rules of §§ 416.1806 through 416.1835 of this part.

### 20 CFR 416.1806

https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-R/section-416.1806

> (a) We will consider someone to be your spouse (and therefore consider you to be married) for SSI purposes if— (1) You are legally married under the laws of the State where your and his or her permanent home is (or was when you lived together); (2) We have decided that either of you is entitled to husband's or wife's Social Security insurance benefits as the spouse of the other (this decision will not affect your SSI benefits for any month before it is made); or (3) You and an unrelated person of the opposite sex are living together in the same household at or after the time you apply for SSI benefits, and you both lead people to believe that you are husband and wife.
>
> (b) if more than one person would qualify as your husband or wife under paragraph (a) of this section, we will consider the person you are presently living with to be your spouse for SSI purposes.

### 20 CFR 416.1160(d) and 416.1802(b)(1)

> Ineligible spouse means someone who lives with you as your husband or wife and is not eligible for SSI benefits.
>
> (b) If you have an eligible spouse—(1) Counting income. If you apply for or receive SSI benefits and have an eligible spouse as defined in § 416.1801(c), we will count your combined income and calculated the benefit amount for you as a couple. [...]

Federal benefit rates for the companion cases are from SSA's "SSI Federal Payment Amounts" table (https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/SSIamts.html, read 2026-10-12): 1986 $336.00 and $504.00; 2026 $994.00 and $1,491.00.

## Required outputs and mapping

Period: Month. Entity: Person, with an explicit same-household spouse relationship.

1. `ssi_spousal_deeming_applies`, Judgment (416.1163(d)): the ineligible spouse's income remaining after 416.1163(b)-(c) allocations is more than the couple rate less the individual rate. "Not more than" is the no-deeming side, so equality means no deeming.
2. `ssi_benefit_under_couple_computation`, Money (416.1163(d)(2)): couple rate less the couple's combined countable income (both spouses' remaining unearned and earned income combined, with the 416.1112 and 416.1124 exclusions applied once to the combined amounts). Floor at zero.
3. `ssi_benefit_without_spousal_deeming`, Money (416.1163(e)(2), second limb): individual rate less only the claimant's own countable income. Floor at zero.
4. `ssi_benefit_with_ineligible_spouse`, Money (416.1163(e)(2)): the lesser of outputs 2 and 3 when output 1 holds; output 3 otherwise.
5. (416.1163(f)(5)) While the $30 Federal benefit rate applies, no spousal income is deemed for eligibility or amount: the benefit is the $30 rate less only the claimant's own countable income. Import the $30 rate from `us/statutes/42/1382/e/1`.
6. `is_ssi_eligible_spouse`, Judgment (416.1801(c)): the person is eligible for SSI, is the spouse of another person eligible for SSI (416.1806), and lived in the same household with that person on the dates in (c)(3). Eligibility for SSI and the dated living-together facts are leaf inputs.
7. `is_ssi_spouse`, Judgment (416.1806): any of (a)(1)-(3), with (b) choosing the person presently lived with when more than one qualifies. Each condition is its own leaf input.
8. `is_ssi_ineligible_spouse`, Judgment (416.1160(d)): lives with the claimant as husband or wife and is not eligible for SSI. A spouse who is aged, blind or disabled but fails the citizenship or qualified-noncitizen condition is not eligible for SSI, so is an ineligible spouse.

Output 4 must never exceed output 3; this is the rule PolicyEngine-US lacked.

## Pasteable review_finding

```text
Encode 20 CFR 416.1163(d), (e)(2) and (f)(5) as a signed module at us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1163.yaml (corpus citation us/regulation/20/416/1163), and 416.1801(c), 416.1806 and 416.1160(d) at us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1801.yaml, 1806.yaml and 1160.yaml (corpus citations us/regulation/20/416/1801, /1806, /1160). No module for any 20 CFR part 416 section exists on rulespec-us origin/main 16a667719. Complete and sign the source bundle before dispatch: the pinned corpus ref 8f7d60aac has these rows in 2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl (lines 4, 6, 12, 14), but the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap does not include that scope. Do not create unsupported citations.

Required Person/Month outputs, each with a verbatim proof excerpt: ssi_spousal_deeming_applies (Judgment, 416.1163(d): remaining spouse income after allocations is more than the couple rate less the individual rate; equality is no deeming); ssi_benefit_under_couple_computation (couple rate less combined countable income, floored at 0); ssi_benefit_without_spousal_deeming (individual rate less only own countable income, floored at 0); ssi_benefit_with_ineligible_spouse (the lesser of the two when deeming applies, per 416.1163(e)(2) 'cannot be higher than it would be if deeming did not apply', otherwise the no-deeming amount); the 416.1163(f)(5) rule that no spousal income is deemed while the $30 rate applies; is_ssi_spouse (416.1806(a)(1)-(3) and (b)); is_ssi_eligible_spouse (416.1801(c)(1)-(3)); is_ssi_ineligible_spouse (416.1160(d)).

Import Federal benefit rates from us/statutes/42/1382/b and us/statutes/42/1382f/a, and the $30 rate from us/statutes/42/1382/e/1. Countable income under 416.1112/416.1124 and the 416.1163(b)-(c) allocations may be exact leaf inputs until those sections are encoded; say so in each leaf's description. Spouse, marriage and living-together facts are leaf inputs named for their legal conditions. Never use tax filing roles, tax dependency or the age order of adults in a tax unit as a proxy for them. A spouse who is aged, blind or disabled but not eligible for SSI (for example on citizenship) is an ineligible spouse.

Add every companion case in this issue. Expectations are hand-computed from the CFR text, the 416.1163(g) examples and SSA's published Federal benefit rates, not from either engine. Refresh rulespec/corpus/rules-engine/encoder refs at dispatch; generated content requires the protected signer and a separately approved billed encoder run. After encoding, register pending oracle coverage for the new outputs and point the PolicyEngine adapter at ssi_if_takes_up, uncapped_ssi_without_spousal_deeming and ssi_claim_is_joint.
```

items.body:
Dispatch-ready encoding debt for SSI parent-to-child income deeming, and for the ineligible-parent and ineligible-child definitions it uses. The companion PolicyEngine change is PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10159, which cites this issue as `axiom: <this issue> queued`. Related issues:

- #1706: spousal deeming (416.1163) and the SSI couple definitions. The ineligible-child allocation in 416.1165(b) is "as described in § 416.1163(b)", so the two should share one allocation rule.
- #1626: parental resource deeming (416.1202(b)). It uses the same parents.

All three have the same corpus blocker. No handwritten RuleSpec has been created.

## Encoding debt and search evidence

Before #10159, PolicyEngine-US grouped parent-to-child deeming by tax unit:

- **Parents.** The deemed parents were the tax unit's non-disabled members flagged as parents. That included grandparents and other parents in the tax unit, included parents living in another household, and left out stepparents and parents filed in another tax unit.
- **Ineligible children.** Every tax-unit child was allocated, including cousins and grandchildren. Half-siblings claimed elsewhere were not.
- **Living allowance.** It was the couple rate when two "parents" were in the tax unit.
- **Division.** Deemed income was split among every disabled child in the tax unit.
- **Status.** No citizenship or qualified-noncitizen test was applied, either to the eligible child or to a parent.

#10159 resolves the child's parents and siblings from relationships, following 416.1160(d). The rules below are what an Axiom module must encode so that the two engines can be compared.

The tracked tree of rulespec-us `origin/main` at `4b35d0872d` (`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main`) holds these SSI modules:

- `us/statutes/42/1382` (with `a/` and `e/`), `1382a/b`, `1382b`, `1382c/a` and `1382f`;
- `us/statutes/42/416`.

Nothing is under `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/`. An issue search for `416.1165` and `parent-to-child deeming` finds only #1626 and #1706. Neither encodes 416.1165.

New modules and companion fixtures:

- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1165.yaml` and `1165.test.yaml`, corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1165`.
- The ineligible-parent and ineligible-child definitions of 416.1160(d), corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1160`. Put them in a `1160.yaml` module shared with #1706, or in `1165.yaml` with a 416.1160(d) proof excerpt.
- The child definition of 416.1856 (via 416.1101), corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1856`.
- The ineligible-child allocation of 416.1163(b)(1)-(2), to be shared with #1706.
- Imports: the Federal benefit rates from `us/statutes/42/1382/b` and `us/statutes/42/1382f/a`. Treat the parents' income after the 416.1161(a) exclusions as exact, legally scoped leaf inputs until 416.1161 is encoded.
- Relationships: model parenthood (natural, adoptive, step) and co-residence (416.1851, 416.1167) as relationships. Do not substitute tax-unit membership, tax dependency or tax roles for them.

## Corpus and signed encoder blocker

The rulespec-us toolchain (`.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml` at `4b35d0872d`) pins:

- `axiom_corpus_ref` `8f7d60aaced28ee4252b9237f9d6e02360dc34bc`;
- axiom-encode `0.2.2092`, ref `3bf5a2afbff0391261ad65bd7497f1b0efaaff85`;
- rules engine ref `89571cc2a938707fd60a5489b951135345697296`.

At that corpus ref, `data/corpus/provisions/us/regulation/2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl` has 14 rows:

- line 4 `416/1160`, line 5 `416/1161`, line 6 `416/1163`, line 7 `416/1167`, line 9 `416/1202`, line 14 `416/1806`;
- no row for `416/1165` or `416/1856`.

axiom-corpus `origin/main` (`56592c88b`, 2026-10-12) has no provision row for `us/regulation/20/416/1165` in any file. `manifests/program-bundles/ssi.yaml` (as of 2026-10-06) lists `us/regulation/20/416/1165` in scope for the screener tier, with `source_url: null`.

As #1626 records, the pinned release manifest `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap` does not include the part-416 regulation scope. Before any dispatch:

1. ingest 416.1165 and 416.1856;
2. publish them in a signed release;
3. re-pin.

Do not dispatch with an invented citation. Follow #1403 and #1416: generated content must come from the signed encoder with its protected signer, and the billed encoder run needs its own approval.

## Regulation (verbatim)

The source is eCFR title 20, versioner XML API, date 2026-09-01, retrieved 2026-10-12. The text is identical to https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/section-416.1165.

### 20 CFR 416.1165 How we deem income to you from your ineligible parent(s)

> If you are a child living with your parents, we apply the deeming rules to you through the month in which you reach age 18. We follow the rules in paragraphs (a) through (e) of this section to determine your eligibility. To determine your benefit amount, we follow the rules in paragraph (f) of this section. The rules in paragraph (g) of this section apply to changes in your family situation. Paragraph (i) of this section discusses the conditions under which we will not deem your ineligible parents' income to you if you are a disabled child living with your parents.
>
> (a) Determining your ineligible parent's income. We first determine how much current monthly earned and unearned income your ineligible parents have, using the appropriate exclusions in § 416.1161(a).
>
> (b) Allocations for ineligible children. We next deduct an allocation for each ineligible child in the household as described in § 416.1163(b).
>
> (c) Allocations for aliens who are sponsored by and have income deemed from your ineligible parent. We also deduct an allocation for eligible aliens who have been sponsored by and have income deemed from your ineligible parent as described in § 416.1163(c).
>
> (d) Allocations for your ineligible parent(s). We next deduct allocations for your parent(s). We do not deduct an allocation for a parent who is receiving public income-maintenance payments (see § 416.1142(a)). The allocations are calculated as follows:
>
> (1) We first deduct $20 from the parents' combined unearned income, if any. If they have less than $20 in unearned income, we subtract the balance of the $20 from their combined earned income.
>
> (2) Next, we subtract $65 plus one-half the remainder of their earned income.
>
> (3) We total the remaining earned and unearned income and subtract—
>
> (i) The Federal benefit rate for the month for a couple if both parents live with you; or
>
> (ii) The Federal benefit rate for the month for an individual if only one parent lives with you.
>
> (e)(1) When you are the only eligible child. If you are the only eligible child in the household, we deem any of your parents' current monthly income that remains to be your unearned income. We combine it with your own unearned income and apply the exclusions in § 416.1124 to determine your countable unearned income in the month. We add this to any countable earned income you may have and subtract the total from the Federal benefit rate for an individual to determine whether you are eligible for benefits.
>
> (2) When you are not the only eligible child. If your parents have more than one eligible child under age 18 in the household, we divide the parental income to be deemed equally among those eligible children.
>
> (3) When one child's income makes that child ineligible. We do not deem more income to an eligible child than the amount which, when combined with the child's own income, reduces his or her SSI benefit to zero. (For purposes of this paragraph, an SSI benefit includes any federally administered State supplement). If the share of parental income that would be deemed to a child makes that child ineligible (reduces the amount to zero) because that child has other countable income, we deem any remaining parental income to other eligible children under age 18 in the household in the manner described in paragraph (e)(2) of this section.

Paragraphs (f) and (g)(1)-(7) set the budget month and the changes in status. The ones that bear on who deems:

> (g)(3) ... If you live with two ineligible parents and one dies, we continue to deem income from the surviving ineligible parent who is also your natural or adoptive parent. If you live with a stepparent following the death of your natural or adoptive parent, we do not deem income from the stepparent.
>
> (g)(4) Ineligible parent and you no longer live in the same household. If your ineligible parent and you no longer live in the same household, we do not deem that parent's income to you to determine your eligibility for SSI benefits beginning with the first month following the month in which one of you leaves the household. We also will not deem income to you from your parent's spouse (i.e., your stepparent) who remains in the household with you if your natural or adoptive parent has permanently left the household. ...
>
> (g)(6) You become subject to the $30 Federal benefit rate. If you become a resident of a medical treatment facility and the $30 Federal benefit rate applies, we do not deem your ineligible parent's income to you ...
>
> (i) Disabled child under age 18. If you are a disabled child under the age of 18 living with your parents, we will not deem your parents' income to you if— (1) You previously received a reduced SSI benefit while a resident of a medical treatment facility, as described in § 416.414; (2) You are eligible for medical assistance under a Medicaid State home care plan approved by the Secretary under the provisions of section 1915(c) or authorized under section 1902(e)(3) of the Act; and (3) You would otherwise be ineligible for a Federal SSI benefit because of the deeming of your parents' income or resources.

Paragraph (h) holds Examples 1-4, with 1992 rates of $422 for an individual and $633 for a couple. The companion cases below use them.

### 20 CFR 416.1160(d), definitions for deeming purposes

> Ineligible child means your natural child or adopted child, or the natural or adopted child of your spouse, or the natural or adopted child of your parent or of your parent's spouse (as the term child is defined in § 416.1101 and the term spouse is defined in § 416.1806), who lives in the same household with you, and is not eligible for SSI benefits.
>
> Ineligible parent means a natural or adoptive parent, or the spouse (as defined in § 416.1101) of a natural or adoptive parent, who lives with you and is not eligible for SSI benefits. The income of ineligible parents affects your benefit only if you are a child under age 18.

### 20 CFR 416.1856 Who is considered a child

> We consider you to be a child if— (a)(1) You are under 18 years old; or (2) You are under 22 years old and you are a student regularly attending school or college or training that is designed to prepare you for a paying job; (b) You are not married; and (c) You are not the head of a household.

### POMS

These were read on 2026-10-12 at https://secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0501320500 and the sibling pages.

- **SI 01310.115 A.2:** "For deeming purposes, an eligible child is a natural or adopted child under age 18 who lives in a household with one or both parents, is not married, and is eligible for SSI."
- **SI 01310.115 A.3:** "an ineligible child is either a natural or adopted child of an: Eligible individual or the eligible individual's spouse; or An ineligible parent or the ineligible parent's spouse, who lives in the same household with an eligible individual".
- **SI 01310.140 A:** the parent-to-child deeming household is "The eligible child; and The eligible child's parent(s); and Other children of the parents."
- **SI 01320.500 A.1:** "The income and resources of the spouse of a natural or adoptive parent (stepparent) who lives with the eligible child are deemed to the child only when the natural or adoptive parent also lives in the household with the stepparent and the child."
- **SI 01320.500 B.4**, the parental living allowance, is:
  - "The monthly FBR for a couple if both parents (or one parent and their spouse) live in the household; or
  - The monthly FBR for an individual if only one parent lives in the household; or
  - The monthly FBR for a couple AND the monthly FBR for an individual if both the natural or adoptive parents and the spouse of the natural or adoptive parent (stepparent) live in the household."

  The exception: "A parental living allowance is not deducted for any parent who receives public income maintenance (PIM) payments".
- **SI 01320.500 C, step 9:** "Divide the result of Step 8 by the number of eligible children in the deeming household."
- **SI 01320.550:**
  - B.3: on the death of a natural parent, "we do not deem from the surviving stepparent".
  - B.8: deeming from a stepparent stops after the natural or adoptive parent permanently leaves.
  - B.9: an adopted child does not resume deeming from a former parent.
  - D.7: Kay, an unmarried 15-year-old, deems to her son Ben until her parents adopt him. After that her parents deem to Ben, with an ineligible-child allocation for Kay.

## Required outputs and mapping

The period is Month. Entities: Person for the child outputs, plus an explicit same-household relationship group for parents, parents' spouses and siblings.

1. **`ssi_ineligible_parents`**, the set of people who deem to the child under 416.1160(d). It holds the child's co-resident natural or adoptive parents, and the co-resident spouse (416.1806) of each, who are not eligible for SSI.
   - A stepparent deems only while that natural or adoptive parent lives in the household (SI 01320.500 A.1, 416.1165(g)(3)-(4)).
   - A parent who is eligible for SSI is not an ineligible parent (416.1165(g)(1)). When an eligible parent lives with an ineligible spouse and an eligible child, 416.1166 applies instead. Encode it or declare it as a deferred dependency; do not fold it into 416.1165.
   - A former parent after adoption is not a parent (SI 01320.550 B.9).
   - A minor parent can be an ineligible parent (SI 01320.550 D.7).
2. **`is_eligible_child_for_parental_deeming`**, a Judgment. The child is under 18 (and in the month of turning 18), not married, not the head of a household, eligible for SSI (SI 01310.115 A.2), and living with at least one ineligible parent.
   - SSI eligibility needs the citizenship or qualified-noncitizen condition. Declare the non-income eligibility classification as a dependency rather than treating every disabled child as eligible.
   - Excepted by (g)(6) (the $30 FBR) or by all three conjunctive conditions of (i).
3. **`parental_deeming_ineligible_child_allocations`**, Money. This is the sum of the 416.1163(b) allocation over each ineligible child in the household. An ineligible child is:
   - the eligible child's own child, or
   - a child of any of the child's parents or parents' spouses, whether or not that parent is eligible (416.1160(d));
   - in either case a child under 416.1856 who is not eligible for SSI.

   Each allocation is the couple rate less the individual rate, less the child's own income under 416.1161(c), floored at zero. There is no allocation for a child receiving public income-maintenance payments.

   Cousins, grandchildren and unrelated children in the household are not allocated, whoever claims them for tax purposes. A child claimed in another tax unit is allocated if they live in the household.
4. **`parental_living_allowance`**, Money, under 416.1165(d)(3) and POMS SI 01320.500 B.4:
   - the individual rate for one deeming parent;
   - the couple rate for two;
   - the couple rate plus the individual rate when both natural or adoptive parents and a stepparent deem;
   - no allowance for a parent receiving public income-maintenance payments.
5. **`parental_income_to_deem`**, Money:
   - Take the parents' income after 416.1161(a).
   - Deduct the child allocations from unearned income first, then from earned income (416.1163(b)(3) and Example 4).
   - Apply the $20 exclusion, then $65 and one-half (416.1165(d)(1)-(2)).
   - Subtract the living allowance, flooring at zero.
   - Do not subtract the eligible child's own student earned income exclusion (416.1112(c)(3)) from the parents' income. It applies only to the child's wages.
6. **`income_deemed_from_parents`**, Money:
   - Divide `parental_income_to_deem` equally among the eligible children of the same parents (416.1165(e)(2)). Children of different parents sharing a home are deemed from their own parents only.
   - Apply the (e)(3) cap and redistribution: deem no more than reduces a child's benefit to zero, and give the rest to the other eligible children (POMS SI 01320.500 F.4).

Invariants to state and test:

- The shares deemed to one set of parents' eligible children add up to that set's income to deem, except where (e)(3) caps a share.
- More income for an ineligible child never lowers the deemed amount.
- More parental income never lowers it.
- The deemed amount is never negative.

## Pasteable review_finding

```text
Encode 20 CFR 416.1165 as a signed module at us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1165.yaml (corpus citation us/regulation/20/416/1165), with the 416.1160(d) ineligible-parent and ineligible-child definitions, the 416.1856 child definition, and the 416.1163(b) ineligible-child allocation, shared with #1706. No module for these sections exists on rulespec-us origin/main 4b35d0872d. The pinned corpus ref 8f7d60aac has 416.1160, 416.1161, 416.1163 and 416.1167, but its part-416 file is not in the pinned release, and no corpus file has 416.1165 or 416.1856. Ingest and release them before dispatch. Do not invent citations.

Ineligible parents are the child's co-resident natural or adoptive parents and each one's co-resident spouse who are not eligible for SSI. A stepparent deems only while the natural or adoptive parent lives in the household (POMS SI 01320.500 A.1, 416.1165(g)(3)-(4)). An eligible parent's income is not deemed (416.1165(g)(1)); 416.1166 governs an eligible parent with an ineligible spouse and an eligible child (declare it as a deferred dependency). Do not use tax-unit membership, tax dependency or tax roles for parenthood or co-residence.

Ineligible children are the child's own children and the children of any of the child's parents or parents' spouses who live in the household, are children under 416.1856 and are not eligible for SSI (416.1160(d), POMS SI 01310.115 A.3, SI 01310.140 A). Cousins and grandchildren are not allocated. Each allocation is the couple rate less the individual rate, less the child's own income (416.1163(b)(2), 416.1161(c)), floored at zero, with none for a child receiving public income-maintenance payments.

The living allowance is the individual rate for one deeming parent, the couple rate for two, and the couple rate plus the individual rate for two natural parents and a stepparent (POMS SI 01320.500 B.4, Example F.5), with none for a parent receiving public income-maintenance payments.

Take the parents' income after 416.1161(a). Deduct the allocations from unearned income first, then earned. Apply $20, then $65 and one-half, subtract the living allowance and floor at zero. Divide equally among the eligible children of the same parents (416.1165(e)(2)), and cap and redistribute under (e)(3). An eligible child is under 18, not married, not a household head, eligible for SSI including the citizenship or qualified-noncitizen condition, and lives with an ineligible parent. Exclude children under (g)(6) or all three conditions of (i).

Add every companion case in this issue. Expectations are hand-computed from the CFR, POMS and SSA rate tables, not copied from an engine. Refresh rulespec, corpus, rules-engine and encoder refs at dispatch. Generated content needs the protected signer and a separately approved billed encoder run.
```

items.body:
## Encoding debt

New York's State Supplement Program (SSP) and State Supplemental Personal Needs Allowance (SSPNA) have no RuleSpec module. On `rulespec-us` `main` (`172bf04e4`, 2026-10-14), `us-ny/statutes/` holds only `NYC/` and `TAX/`, `us-ny/regulations/18-nycrr/` only Parts 385 and 387, and `us-ny/policies/otda/` only `snap/` and `tanf-state-plan-2024-2026/`. Searches for "New York SSP", "State Supplement Program", "18 NYCRR 398", "SSPNA" and "209" New York find no New York SSP issue; hits are #1712 (New York HEAP rows), #394 (unrelated) and other states' supplements (#1450, #1708, #1709, #1766, #1767, #1771).

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10158 (open) adds the program to PolicyEngine-US:

- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ny/otda/ssp/`: `ny_ssp`, `ny_ssp_living_arrangement` (formula) and `ny_ssp_care_setting` (input), Person monthly; `ny_ssp_is_minor`, Person yearly.
- **Parameters** under `gov.states.ny.otda.ssp`: increments over the FBR, downstate premiums, the $1 minimum, minor ages and the SSPNA. Congregate-care couple amounts are computed.
- **Tests:** `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ny/otda/ssp/ny_ssp.yaml` (48 cases) and `integration.yaml` (11 cases).
- **Scope:** 2026 amounts from 2026-01-01; earlier years out of scope.

## Module paths and corpus citations

| Proposed module | Provisions | Corpus status |

| `us-ny/statutes/SOS/209.yaml` | (1)(d) facility bar, (2)(a)-(f) standards of need, (2-a) SSPNA, (3) definitions, (4) payment | Needs ingest: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/SOS/209 (Cloudflare; fetch as for `us-ny/statute/LAB/527`) |
| Co-cited for the 2026 amounts | L.2026 ch.56 Part L § 2 (S.9006-C), printed pages 28-29 | Needs ingest: https://nyassembly.gov/leg/?default_fld=&leg_video=&bn=S09006&term=2025&Text=Y. The corpus has `us-ny/statute/bills/2025/s3006` (L.2025 ch.56), whose Part R § 2 sets the 2025 amounts |
| `us-ny/regulations/18-nycrr/398-2/1.yaml` | Definitions (g), (l), (o), (t), (ac) | Part 398 is in no manifest (only Parts 385 and 387); needs ingest: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-york/18-NYCRR-398-2.1 |

I checked the manifests on axiom-corpus `main` (`437198d6c`), not the signed release that rulespec-us pins.

## Source text (verbatim)

**SSL § 209(2)** as amended by L.2026 ch.56 Part L § 2 (deletions omitted; takes effect December 31, 2026):

> (a) On and after January first, two thousand twenty-six, for an eligible individual living alone, $1,081.00; and for an eligible couple living alone, $1,595.00.
> (b) On and after January first, two thousand twenty-six, for an eligible individual living with others with or without in-kind income, $1,017.00; and for an eligible couple living with others with or without in-kind income, $1,537.00.
> (c) On and after January first, two thousand twenty-six, (i) for an eligible individual receiving family care, $1,260.48 if such individual is receiving such care in the city of New York or the county of Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester or Rockland; and (ii) for an eligible couple receiving family care in [...], two times the amount set forth in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph; or (iii) for an eligible individual receiving such care in any other county in the state, $1,222.48; and (iv) [...] two times the amount set forth in subparagraph (iii) of this paragraph.
> (e) On and after January first, two thousand twenty-six, (i) for an eligible individual receiving enhanced residential care, $1,688.00; and (ii) for an eligible couple receiving enhanced residential care, two times the amount set forth in subparagraph (i) of this paragraph.

(d) has the same structure for "an eligible individual receiving residential care, $1,429.00" downstate and "$1,399.00" elsewhere. During 2026 the text in force (L.2025 ch.56 Part R § 2) has the 2025 amounts and:

> (f) The amounts set forth in paragraphs (a) through (e) of this subdivision shall be increased to reflect any increases in federal supplemental security income benefits for individuals or couples which become effective on or after January first, two thousand twenty-six but prior to June thirtieth, two thousand twenty-six.

The 2025 amounts plus the 2026 federal increase ($27; couple $41) give the same 2026 figures; congregate-care couples stay at two times the individual figure.

**SSL § 209(1)(d), (2-a), (3)(b), (4):**

> (d) Any inconsistent provision of this title notwithstanding, an individual shall not be eligible for additional state payments with respect to any month, if throughout such month, (i) he is an inmate of a public institution, or (ii) he is an inmate in a medical facility which is receiving medical assistance payments for him at a level exceeding fifty per cent of the cost of his care, or (iii) he is an inmate in a medical facility which is not certified under the state's medical assistance program. [...]

> a resident of a residential health care facility as defined by section twenty-eight hundred one of the public health law [...] the state payment for personal needs for such persons shall be in the amount of twenty-five dollars a month.

> a resident of an intermediate care facility operated or issued an operating certificate by the office for people with developmental disabilities or a patient of a hospital operated by the office of mental health [...] shall receive a state payment for personal needs in the amount of five dollars a month.

> (b) "Living with others" shall mean [...] with respect to any child who is not the head of a household and who is under the age of eighteen, or under the age of twenty-two if attending school, any living arrangement other than residential care in a facility operated or licensed by an office of the department of mental hygiene.

> 4. An eligible individual or an eligible couple shall be entitled to receive monthly an additional state payment in an amount equal to the difference between the monthly standard of need applicable to such individual or couple and the sum of such individual's or couple's supplemental security income benefit plus countable income.

**18 NYCRR 398-2.1:**

> (g) [...] Countable income is all of a person's income, in cash or in kind, earned and unearned, which is not excluded by federal law or regulation in determining eligibility for SSI.
> (l) [...] An eligible couple consists of two persons, both of whom [...] are in active receipt of SSI as defined in this Part, live together in the same residence [...]
> (o) [...] The FBR is the maximum amount of SSI payable to an individual or couple with no countable income.
> (t) [...] A minor child is a person under age 18, or under age 22 and a student regularly attending school, college, or vocational training and who is neither married nor a head of a household.
> (ac) [...] The State benefit rate is equal to the State standard of need for the recipient's applicable State Living Arrangement minus the FBR or a recipient's monthly Countable Income, whichever is greater.

**398-3.2(b), (d), 398-3.4:**

> (b) be in active receipt of SSI benefits;

> (d) have no countable income, earned or unearned, other than the federal SSI benefit provided to residents of medical facilities for whom the Medical Assistance Program pays at least 50 percent of the cost of care.

> An eligible person who is a resident of a residential health care facility as defined by section 2801 of the Public Health Law receives a $25 monthly benefit. An eligible resident of an intermediate care facility [...] receives a $5 monthly benefit.

**398-4.2(b), 398-4.4(b)-(c), 398-4.6(c):**

> (b) A person is not eligible for SSP benefits if, on the first of the month, the individual is: (1) an inmate of a public institution; or (2) a resident of a medical facility which is receiving medical assistance for the individual at a level exceeding 50 percent of the cost of the individual's care.

> (b) The monthly SSP benefit amount equals the State benefit rate minus the greater of the FBR or countable income. (c) The State benefit rate will be established based on the individual's or the couple's State living arrangement on the first day of the month.

> (c) The minimum monthly benefit issuance for SSP is $1.

**398-4.5:** (a)(1)(vi) "lives with only a foster child;"

> (2) An individual or couple is not considered to be living alone if: (i) the individual lives with an ineligible spouse; (ii) the individual or couple lives with a minor child for whom they have primary responsibility (unless the minor child is a foster child); (iii) the individual is a minor child; [...]

> (b) Living with others. [...] (2) is a minor child who is not living in a congregate care facility. (3) is a minor child living in a congregate care level III facility. [...] (6) is categorized by the SSA as Living in the Household of Another for purposes of SSI benefits.

> After the month of entry into a congregate care level II facility that is classified as an institution for purposes of federal SSI benefits, couples are treated as consisting of two individuals, since couple status can exist only in households, not institutions.

That is (d); (e) repeats it for level III.

## Required outputs

All Person, monthly (minor child yearly).

| Output | PolicyEngine-US | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| Standard of need | `amount.*` and premiums (standard minus FBR) | By arrangement, region (family and residential care) and individual or couple; congregate-care couple = two times the individual standard (209(2)(c)-(e)) |
| Living arrangement (Judgment) | `ny_ssp_living_arrangement`, from `ny_ssp_care_setting` | 398-4.5 category on the first of the month (398-4.4(c)) |
| Minor child (Judgment) | `ny_ssp_is_minor` | 398-2.1(t); lives with others outside certified family or residential care (398-4.5(b)-(d)) |
| Medical-facility bar (Judgment) | facility rows and `NONE` of `ny_ssp_living_arrangement` | No SSP in a public institution or where Medicaid pays over 50 percent (209(1)(d)(i)-(ii); 398-4.2(b)), nor in a medical facility where it pays less (chart footnote 5) |
| SSP (Money) | `ny_ssp` | max(0, standard − (SSI + countable income)) (209(4)), the one-third reduction counting as income (20 CFR 416.1131(a)). Under spousal deeming: max(0, standard − max(own FBR, countable income incl. deemed income)), own FBR = individual FBR, one-third less in another person's household (398-2.1(ac), (g), (o); 398-4.4(b)). A couple's amount is split equally and a positive share below $1 is paid as $1 (398-4.6(c)) |
| SSPNA (Money) | `ny_ssp` (plus `personal_needs.*`) | $25 in a residential health care facility, $5 in an OPWDD intermediate care facility or OMH hospital, none in other medical facilities (209(2-a), 398-3.4); requires SSI and no countable income besides it (398-3.2(b), (d)) |

items.body:
Dispatch-ready encoding debt for the regulation. The statute it implements, 42 USC 1382c(f)(1) and (f)(2), was dispatched to the signed encoder on 2026-10-09 (axiom-encode runs [37983146825](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/actions/runs/37983146825) and [37983156312](https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-encode/actions/runs/37983156312)); both runs were told to defer the statute's "inequitable under the circumstances" exception to `us/regulation/20/416/1202`, which is this issue. No handwritten RuleSpec has been created.

## Encoding debt and search evidence

PolicyEngine-US currently tests a person's own SSI-countable resources against the individual limit, except that it combines resources for an SSI joint claim. It omits resources of an ineligible spouse and parent-to-child resource deeming. The companion PolicyEngine change implements 20 CFR 416.1202(a), (b), and 416.1205; see PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#3557.

I searched the tracked tree of rulespec-us `origin/main` at `16a6677190194da2431a78fcaa5b6548cd0e2845` with `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main`, filtering for SSI, Supplemental Security Income, 20 CFR, part 416, and the relevant section numbers. A bounded `git grep` of tracked federal modules and manifests found no encoding of 20 CFR 416.1202 or 416.1205. The existing `us/regulations/42-cfr/435/120/ssi-mandatory-group.yaml` only encodes the Medicaid obligation for people receiving or deemed to receive SSI; its SSI status is a supplied input. It does not compute SSI resources or SSI resource eligibility. `us/statutes/42/416/l.yaml` concerns a different provision and is not the requested CFR provision.

New modules and companion fixtures:

- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1202.yaml` and `1202.test.yaml`; corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1202`.
- `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/1205.yaml` and `1205.test.yaml`; corpus citation `us/regulation/20/416/1205`.
- Referenced definitions: 20 CFR 416.1856 (child), 416.1851 (household), 416.1806 (spouse), 416.1167 (temporary absence), and 416.1207 (first-moment-of-month resource determination). Import signed modules where available; otherwise declare exact, legally scoped leaf inputs and deferred dependencies. Do not substitute tax filing or tax dependency definitions for these relationships.
- SSA POMS companion guidance: SI 01330.100, .200, .280, .310, and .340. Give any rule that depends on POMS rather than directly on the CFR a POMS proof source.

## Corpus and signed encoder blocker

The rulespec-us toolchain pins corpus release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap` and corpus ref `8f7d60aaced28ee4252b9237f9d6e02360dc34bc`. At that git ref, `data/corpus/provisions/us/regulation/2026-07-23-title-20-part-416.jsonl`, line 9, is `us/regulation/20/416/1202`, source format `ecfr-xml`, source as of `2026-07-14`. Its operative text matches the eCFR XML retrieved for `2026-10-05` on `2026-10-09`. However, the pinned release manifest `manifests/releases/us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap.json` does not include the `2026-07-23-title-20-part-416` regulation scope. Existence at the pinned git ref does not make this provision dispatchable from the pinned release.

That partial part-416 corpus snapshot also includes 416.1167, 416.1207, and 416.1806. It contains no section row for 416.1205, 416.1851, or 416.1856. A bounded search of all federal regulation JSONL files at the pinned ref found no alternate 416.1205 or 416.1856 row. POMS proof sources also need ingestion or confirmation in the dispatch source bundle. The signed encoder is therefore blocked on completing the corpus source bundle and making it available in the pinned signed release. Do not dispatch with an invented citation or replace the legally necessary definitions with an opaque aggregate.

The current rulespec-us `.axiom/workflow-toolchain.toml` names axiom-encode `0.2.2092`, ref `3bf5a2afbff0391261ad65bd7497f1b0efaaff85`, and rules engine ref `89571cc2a938707fd60a5489b951135345697296`. Refresh and verify all refs at dispatch time. Follow issues #1403 and #1416: generated content must come from the signed encoder with its protected signer, and the billed encoder run needs its own approval.

The companion PolicyEngine pull request cites this issue as `axiom: <this issue> queued`, with the corpus blocker above.

## Regulation (verbatim)

The primary source is eCFR, title 20 current through `2026-10-05`, retrieved `2026-10-09` using the versioner XML API. Official SSA CFR pages provide an independently accessible copy:

- https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-L/section-416.1202
- https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1202.htm
- https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-20/chapter-III/part-416/subpart-L/section-416.1205
- https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1205.htm

### 20 CFR 416.1202

> (a) Married individual. In the case of an individual who is living with a person not eligible under this part and who is considered to be the husband or wife of such individual under the criteria in §§ 416.1802 through 416.1835 of this part, such individual's resources shall be deemed to include any resources, not otherwise excluded under this subpart, of such spouse whether or not such resources are available to such individual. In addition to the exclusions listed in § 416.1210, we also exclude the following items:
>
> (1) Pension funds that the ineligible spouse may have. Pension funds are defined as funds held in individual retirement accounts (IRA), as described by the Internal Revenue Code, or in work-related pension plans (including such plans for self-employed persons, sometimes referred to as Keogh plans);
>
> (2) For 9 months beginning with the month following the month of receipt, the unspent portion of any retroactive payment of special pay an ineligible spouse received from one of the uniformed services pursuant to 37 U.S.C. 310; and
>
> (3) For 9 months beginning with the month following the month of receipt, the unspent portion of any retroactive payment of family separation allowance an ineligible spouse received from one of the uniformed services pursuant to 37 U.S.C. 427 as a result of deployment to or service in a combat zone (as defined in § 416.1160(d)).
>
> (b) Child—(1) General. In the case of a child (as defined in § 416.1856) who is under age 18, we will deem to that child any resources, not otherwise excluded under this subpart, of his or her ineligible parent who is living in the same household with him or her (as described in § 416.1851). We also will deem to the child the resources of his or her ineligible stepparent. As used in this section, the term “parent” means the natural or adoptive parent of a child, and the term “stepparent” means the spouse (as defined in § 416.1806) of such natural or adoptive parent who is living in the same household with the child and parent. We will deem to a child the resources of his or her parent and stepparent whether or not those resources are available to him or her. We will deem to a child the resources of his or her parent and stepparent only to the extent that those resources exceed the resource limits described in § 416.1205. (If the child is living with only one parent, we apply the resource limit for an individual. If the child is living with both parents, or the child is living with one parent and a stepparent, we apply the resource limit for an individual and spouse.) We will not deem to a child the resources of his or her parent or stepparent if the child is excepted from deeming under paragraph (b)(2) of this section. In addition to the exclusions listed in § 416.1210, we also exclude the following items:
>
> (i) Pension funds of an ineligible parent (or stepparent). Pension funds are defined as funds held in IRAs, as described by the Internal Revenue Code, or in work-related pension plans (including such plans for self-employed persons, sometimes referred to as Keogh plans);
>
> (ii) For 9 months beginning with the month following the month of receipt, the unspent portion of any retroactive payment of special pay an ineligible parent (or stepparent) received from one of the uniformed services pursuant to 37 U.S.C. 310; and
>
> (iii) For 9 months beginning with the month following the month of receipt, the unspent portion of any retroactive payment of family separation allowance an ineligible parent (or stepparent) received from one of the uniformed services pursuant to 37 U.S.C. 427 as a result of deployment to or service in a combat zone (as defined in § 416.1160(d)).
>
> (2) Disabled child under age 18. In the case of a disabled child under age 18 who is living in the same household with his or her parents, the deeming provisions of paragraph (b)(1) of this section shall not apply if such child—
>
> (i) Previously received a reduced SSI benefit while a resident of a medical treatment facility, as described in § 416.414;
>
> (ii) Is eligible for medical assistance under a Medicaid State home care plan approved by the Secretary under the provisions of section 1915(c) or authorized under section 1902(e)(3) of the Act; and
>
> (iii) Would otherwise be ineligible because of the deeming of his or her parents' resources or income.
>
> (c) Applicability. When used in this subpart L, the term individual refers to an eligible aged, blind, or disabled person, and also includes a person whose resources are deemed to be the resources of such individual (as provided in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section).

### 20 CFR 416.1205

> (a) Individual with no eligible spouse. An aged, blind, or disabled individual with no spouse is eligible for benefits under title XVI of the Act if his or her nonexcludable resources do not exceed $1,500 prior to January 1, 1985, and all other eligibility requirements are met. An individual who is living with an ineligible spouse is eligible for benefits under title XVI of the Act if his or her nonexcludable resources, including the resources of the spouse, do not exceed $2,250 prior to January 1, 1985, and all other eligibility requirements are met.
>
> (b) Individual with an eligible spouse. An aged, blind, or disabled individual who has an eligible spouse is eligible for benefits under title XVI of the Act if their nonexcludable resources do not exceed $2,250 prior to January 1, 1985, and all other eligibility requirements are met.
>
> (c) Effective January 1, 1985 and later. The resources limits and effective dates for January 1, 1985 and later are as follows:

| Effective date | Individual | Individual and spouse |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Jan. 1, 1985 | $1,600 | $2,400 |
| Jan. 1, 1986 | 1,700 | $2,550 |
| Jan. 1, 1987 | 1,800 | $2,700 |
| Jan. 1, 1988 | 1,900 | $2,850 |
| Jan. 1, 1989 | 2,000 | $3,000 |

### Definitions and timing

20 CFR 416.1856, https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1856.htm:

> We consider you to be a child if—
>
> (a)(1) You are under 18 years old; or
>
> (2) You are under 22 years old and you are a student regularly attending school or college or training that is designed to prepare you for a paying job;
>
> (b) You are not married; and
>
> (c) You are not the head of a household.

416.1202(b) additionally requires age under 18; the student extension in 416.1856 does not extend parent resource deeming to ages 18–21.

20 CFR 416.1207(a), https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1207.htm:

> Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month. A resource determination is based on what assets an individual has, what their values are, and whether or not they are excluded as of the first moment of the month.

20 CFR 416.1167(a), (b), (c), https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/cfr20/416/416-1167.htm:

> (a) General. During a temporary absence, we continue to consider the absent person a member of the household. A temporary absence occurs when—
>
> (1) You, your ineligible spouse, parent, or an ineligible child leaves the household but intends to and does return in the same month or the month immediately following; or
>
> (2) You enter a medical treatment facility and are eligible for either benefit payable under § 416.212. We consider your absence to be temporary through the last month benefits under § 416.212 were paid unless you were discharged from the facility in the following month. In that case, we consider your absence to be temporary through the date of discharge.

> If you are an eligible child who is away at school but comes home on some weekends or lengthy holidays and if you are subject to the control of your parents, we consider you temporarily absent from your parents' household. However, if you are not subject to parental control, we do not consider your absence temporary and we do not deem parental income (or resources) to you. Being subject to parental control affects deeming to you only if you are away at school.
>
> If your ineligible spouse or parent is absent from the household due solely to a duty assignment as a member of the Armed Forces on active duty, we continue to consider that person to be living in the same household as you, absent evidence to the contrary. If we determine that during such an absence, evidence indicates that your spouse or parent should no longer be considered to be living in the same household as you, then deeming will cease. When such evidence exists, we determine the month in which your spouse or parent should no longer be considered to be living in the same household as you and stop deeming his or her income and resources beginning with the month following that month.

Do not equate physical absence with termination of household membership. In particular, a medical-facility residence does not stop deeming if it is an absence qualifying under 416.1167(a)(2). An adjudicated temporary-absence input must certify one of these exact conditions, rather than merely labelling a move as temporary.

### POMS instructions and examples

SI 01330.100, https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501330100:

> The resources of an individual who is living with an ineligible spouse include the resources of the spouse, whether or not they are available to the applicant /recipient.

SI 01330.200(B), https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501330200:

> If there is more than one SSI eligible child under age 18 in the household, equally divide the value of the deemed resources among those children.
>
> If an eligible child is later determined ineligible for any reason or is no longer subject to deeming (e.g., after attainment of age 18), divide the value of the deemed resources among the remaining eligible children, effective with the first month the child is ineligible or no longer subject to deeming.

SI 01330.310, https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501330310:

> If a child under age 18 lives in the same household with a parent(s) applying for SSI or an eligible parent(s), determine the countable resources of the parent(s) by following the guidelines in SI 01110.001 ff. and SI 01330.100 ff., as applicable.
>
> If the parent(s) meets the resource eligibility requirement, do not deem the value of any parental resources to the child.
>
> If the parent(s) does not meet the resource eligibility requirements, follow the usual parent-to-child resource deeming rules in SI 01330.200 ff. to determine the value of the deemed parental resources.

The requested SI 01330.210 URL returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-09. The current SSA SI 01330.000 table of contents, revised 2026-06-03, lists .200 followed by .220, .260, and .280, and contains no .210. This issue makes no claim about unavailable .210 text. Current .310 and .340 resolve the eligible-parent case directly.

SI 01310.145(A)(1), https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501310145, clarifies the current stepparent rule:

> Parent-to-child deeming from a stepparent does not apply when the natural or adoptive parent has permanently left the household. Treat any absence by a natural or adoptive parent as permanent unless it is considered a temporary absence according to the instructions in SI 01310.165.

SI 01330.120(A)(1) and .220(A)(1) identify September 1, 1987 as the effective date of the pension-fund deeming exclusion. If historical versions are encoded, do not apply that exclusion before its effective date. The companion PolicyEngine cases are all after that date.

## Required outputs and mapping

Period: Month. Entity: Person for individual outputs, with an explicit same-household parent/spouse relationship group where needed. The PolicyEngine adapter may use its existing tax-unit parent roles and marital-unit spouse roles, but those adapter conventions are not legal definitions.

1. `ssi_individual_resource_limit` and `ssi_couple_resource_limit`, Money, from 416.1205(c), including the effective dates above. The couple limit applies both to two eligible spouses and to an eligible individual with an ineligible spouse.
2. `ssi_spouse_resources_subject_to_deeming`, Money: same-household ineligible spouse's otherwise countable resources, removing the additional 416.1202(a)(1)–(3) exclusions. The result is nonnegative and does not depend on whether the resources are available to the eligible individual.
3. `ssi_parent_resources_subject_to_deeming`, Money: resources of legally qualifying parents/stepparents in the same household, applying the general exclusions and additional 416.1202(b)(1)(i)–(iii) exclusions. An SSI application or aged/blind/disabled status alone does not establish an eligible parent; apply SI 01330.310 before classifying the parent.
4. `ssi_parent_resource_allowance`, Money: individual limit for one resident parent; couple limit for two resident parents or one parent plus resident stepparent. Read the same 416.1205 outputs as the final resource test, so a counterfactual limit change changes the allowance too.
5. `ssi_resources_deemed_from_parents`, Money: nonnegative parental excess over the allowance; zero when the parent(s) meets the resource requirement under SI 01330.310; zero for a child outside the 416.1856 definition/under-18 requirement or excepted under all three conjunctive elements of 416.1202(b)(2). Split excess equally across SSI-eligible children, redetermining the remaining set when a child is ineligible, following SI 01330.200(B) and the Goode example. Declare any non-resource SSI eligibility classification dependency instead of treating all disabled children as eligible automatically.
6. `ssi_resources_for_resource_test`, Money: individual own countable resources plus applicable spouse or parent deemed resources; combined own resources for an eligible couple. Do not double-count a spouse in both the combined resource base and the deemed resource addend.
7. `meets_ssi_resource_test`, Judgment: compare the resource base with the appropriate limit using inclusive `<=`. An eligible individual living with an ineligible spouse uses the couple limit even when no joint SSI claim is made. Children use the individual limit.

The pension exclusion applies to the ineligible deemor's pension funds; it is not a general exclusion of the eligible individual's own retirement assets. The two military payment exclusions last nine months beginning with the month after receipt. They must be treated as excluded asset amounts, not current military income, and cannot reduce deemed resources below zero.

The PolicyEngine model is annual and uses tax-unit parents/marital-unit spouses. Full SSI eligibility also depends on income, citizenship, residence, and other criteria. Resource formulas must not recursively call final child eligibility when forming the parent resource pool or eligible-child denominator. SI 01330.310 and .340 establish how to test applying/eligible parents' resources without that recursion. Aged/blind/disabled status is an existing PolicyEngine proxy, not the complete legal meaning of “eligible.”

Temporal questions should be adjudicated monthly in RuleSpec; do not infer a cessation date from an annual age snapshot. The PolicyEngine Month formula reads the annual `age` input at `period.this_year`, because age is a level and must not be apportioned across months.

items.body:
## Encoding debt

`us-co/regulations/9-ccr-2503-5/3.549.yaml` encodes the client disregards (3.549(A)) and spousal deeming (3.549(C)-(D), (F)). It defers three things that PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10161 now computes.

1. **Parental deeming, 3.549(E).** Deferred output `and_cs_grant_payment_after_all_deemed_income` ("requires parental deeming, sponsor deeming ..."). No rule deems a parent's income to an AND-CS client who is an unemancipated child.
2. **The 3.549(H) total.** Nothing sums the client's countable income with income deemed from a spouse or parents and subtracts it from the grant standard. `and_cs_authorized_grant_payment_before_deemed_income` stops before deeming.
3. **The couple's combined $20.** `and_cs_deemed_spouse_unearned_income_under_standard_method` reduces the spouse's unearned income by `20 - and_cs_client_unearned_income_disregard_used`. When 3.549(A)(2)(f) has applied part of the client's unused disregard to the client's earnings, that part is offered again to the spouse, and the couple gets more than the "combined $20.00 disregard" of 3.549(D)(2).

Two more findings in the same module:

4. **Effective dates.** Every 3.549 version starts `2016-10-01`. The text these rules encode first took effect **March 1, 2020** (ruleVersionId 8577, PDF page 76-77). From March 2, 2014 through February 29, 2020 the section was 3.545 [Eff. 3/2/14] (ruleVersionId 8443, PDF page 63). It had no client earned income calculation (3.549(A)(1)). Its (F) read: "If a spouse or parent is receiving assistance under another category of public assistance, SSI benefits, or medical assistance, the income from those benefits shall not be considered as available to the client". That excludes only the benefit income. It has no SSI-limit test and does not exempt the recipient's other income.
5. **Spouse inputs.** `and_cs_standard_spouse_deeming_method_applies` takes `spouse_income_is_no_greater_than_ssi_limit` as a leaf input. The rule does not define "the SSI limit". PolicyEngine reads it as SSI's income test for an individual: countable income after the 20 CFR 416.1112/416.1124 exclusions no greater than the individual federal benefit rate. That is an interpretation, so the leaf input can stay, but the summary should say the term is undefined.

## Law (verbatim)

9 CCR 2503-5, ruleVersionId 12428, https://www.sos.state.co.us/CCR/GenerateRulePdf.do?fileName=9+CCR+2503-5&ruleVersionId=12428, PDF pages 93-96:

> C. A portion of the earned income of an AND-CS client's spouse shall be deemed to the client, as follows: 1. Determine the spouse's monthly gross income. 2. Deduct $65.00 from the monthly gross income; and, 3. Divide the remainder by two (2). 4. The result is the amount deemed to the client.

> D. A portion of the unearned income for the AND-CS client's spouse shall be deemed to the client, as follows: 1. Determine the spouse's monthly gross unearned income. 2. Deduct any remaining unearned income disregard remaining from the client or $20.00, whichever is less. A couple shall be allowed a combined $20.00 disregard, which is split between the client and the spouse. 3. The result is countable unearned income and is deemed to the client.

> E. When the AND-CS client is an unemancipated child under eighteen (18) years of age, the earned and unearned income of the child and the child's parents shall be subject to disregards and deeming, as outlined above. The parents' income shall be deemed using the same calculations as a spouse.

> F. If a spouse or parent is receiving Adult Financial grant payments, SSI benefits, or Medicaid assistance and has income no greater than the SSI limit, their income shall not be considered as available to the AND-CS client and shall not be deemed. If a spouse is institutionalized and the client has retained the MMMNA, the MMMNA shall be deducted from the institutionalized spouse's total income.

> H. The county department shall determine all countable earned and unearned income available from the client, the spouse/parents, and the sponsor(s). The total shall be deducted from the AND-CS grant standard to determine the client's grant payment amount. If the grant payment is less than the AND-CS payment floor standard as outlined in section 3.546, a state supplementary payment will be issued to raise the grant payment to meet the payment floor standard.

## Why this is not a PR

Content must come from the signed encoder (`targeted-signed-reencode.yml`). A signed run is OpenAI-billed, and each one needs Max's approval, so this is queued rather than dispatched. Sponsor deeming (3.549(G)) and the MMMNA allocation stay deferred. Their deferral reasons in the module are accurate.

## Required outputs

1. `and_cs_deemed_parent_earned_income`: when the client is an unemancipated child under 18, (parents' combined gross earned income − 65) / 2, floored at 0, excluding any parent exempt under (F).
2. `and_cs_deemed_parent_unearned_income`: parents' combined gross unearned income less the child's remaining disregard (min of $20 and 20 − the child's disregard used), floored at 0, excluding any parent exempt under (F).
3. `and_cs_total_countable_income_after_deeming` (3.549(H)): the client's countable income (3.549(A), SSI included) plus deemed spouse and parent income (sponsor deeming as a declared leaf or deferred).
4. `and_cs_grant_payment_after_deemed_income` (3.549(H)): `max(0, and_cs_total_grant_standard − total)`, with the payment floor applied only when the total is below the grant standard (see the companion floor issue).
5. The spouse-deeming disregard reduced by the part of the $20 the client applied to earnings under (A)(2)(f), so the couple's total never exceeds $20.
6. `effective_from: '2020-03-01'` for the 3.549 text; pre-March-2020 versions, if encoded, follow 3.545 (ruleVersionId 8443).

## review_finding (paste)

> 9 CCR 2503-5 3.549 (corpus us-co/regulation/9-ccr-2503-5/3.549) defers parental deeming and the 3.549(H) total (deferred output and_cs_grant_payment_after_all_deemed_income). Encode 3.549(E): for an unemancipated child client under 18, deem the parents' combined income "using the same calculations as a spouse" — earned (gross − $65) / 2 per 3.549(C), unearned less the child's remaining share of the $20 per 3.549(D)(2) — excluding a parent who receives Adult Financial grant payments, SSI or Medicaid with income no greater than the SSI limit (3.549(F)). Encode 3.549(H): total countable income = client countable income (3.549(A), with SSI added back) + deemed spouse income + deemed parent income; grant = max(0, grant standard − total), raised to the 3.546(E) payment floor only when total < grant standard (3.520.781(A)). Under 3.549(D)(2) the couple's combined disregard is $20: subtract the client's (A)(2)(f) earnings use as well as the unearned use before offering the remainder to the spouse. The 3.549 text took effect 2020-03-01 (ruleVersionId 8577); set effective_from accordingly, not 2016-10-01 (the prior 3.545 [Eff. 3/2/14] had no client earned-income calculation and its (F) excluded only the benefit income).

## Companion tests (2026; expectations from the rule text, the same ground truth as PolicyEngine #10161's YAML)

| Case | Inputs (monthly) | Expected | PE-US YAML |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Ineligible spouse below SSI's deeming threshold | client SSI only; spouse earns 300, no assistance | deemed earned 117.50 | `co_state_supplement_deemed_income` Case 1 |
| B. Split disregard | client SSDI 300 (married share 10 used); spouse pension 400, no assistance | client countable unearned 290; deemed unearned 390; total other than SSI 680 | Case 2; `co_state_supplement_countable_income` Case 4 |
| C. Spouse on Medicaid within the SSI limit | as B, spouse on Medicaid (SSI countable 380 ≤ 994) | deemed 0 | Case 3 |
| D. Child, two parents, no assistance | child SSI only; parent 1 earns 2,000; parent 2 none | deemed parent earned 967.50 | Case 5 |
| E. Child, earning parent on Medicaid | as D, parent 1 on Medicaid (SSI countable 957.50 ≤ 994) | deemed 0 | Case 6 |
| F. Child, one parent with a pension | child SSI only; parent pension 500, no assistance | deemed parent unearned 480 | Case 7 |
| G. Spouse on Medicaid, SSI deems | client no income, SSI 783.50; spouse earns 1,500 on Medicaid | deemed 0; grant 994 − 783.50 = 210.50 | `co_state_supplement` Case 29 |
| H. Same spouse not on assistance | as G without Medicaid | deemed 717.50; total 1,501 ≥ 994; grant 0, no floor | Case 30 |
| I. Combined $20 cap | married client: interest 10, earnings 200, SSI 0; spouse pension 50, no assistance | client uses 10 on interest and 10 on earnings ((200 − 65 − 10) / 2 = 62.50); remaining for spouse 0; deemed unearned 50 | `co_state_supplement_deemed_income` Case 8 |
