## Encoding debt and defects

`us-co/regulations/9-ccr-2503-5/3.534.yaml` encodes part of OAP spousal deeming. PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10176 now applies 3.534(A)-(C) to every OAP client.

1. **Unearned deeming is deferred.** The deferred output is `spouse_deemed_unearned_income`, with reason "Calculation requires the SSI benefit standard defined in uncopied section 3.510". 3.510 is now in the corpus (`us-co/regulations/9-ccr-2503-5/3.510.yaml` exists but has no SSI benefit standard output). 3.534(B) deems the spouse's unearned income less the OAP grant standard, less an allocation for each dependent child in the spouse's household, less the spouse's medical payments for uninsured dependents, and less court-ordered support obligations. The SSI benefit standard enters only through the child allocation ("half the maximum SSI grant benefit standard ... less the dependent child's own income"). It can be a declared input or a parameter ($994/month for an individual in 2026).
2. **Deemed earnings can be negative.** `spouse_deemed_earned_income` is `(spouse_gross_countable_earned_income_including_court_garnished_wages − 65) / 2` with no floor. A spouse earning $30/month deems −$17.50, which would reduce the client's countable income. 3.534(A) deducts $65 and halves "the remainder", so a spouse earning under $65 deems nothing.
3. **No total.** 3.534(A)(4) and (B)(7) say deemed income "shall be considered income to the client and shall be deducted, together with any other income, from the grant of the client". No rule adds deemed income to `oap_total_countable_income_under_3_533`. 3.532 takes `client_total_countable_income_for_oap` as a leaf.
4. **Effective dates.** Every 3.534 version starts `2016-10-01`. The text encoded took effect **March 1, 2020** (ruleVersionId 8577, PDF pages 63-64). From March 2, 2014 through February 29, 2020 (ruleVersionId 8443, PDF pages 50-51), 3.534 deemed income "from a non-recipient spouse to a recipient spouse", with no exemption for a spouse on SSI or Medicaid.
5. **"The OAP limit" is undefined.** `spouse_income_not_deemed` takes `spouse_income_no_greater_than_oap_limit` as a leaf. PolicyEngine reads the limit as the OAP grant standard, applied to the spouse's own total countable income under 3.533 with SSI included. That is an interpretation, so the leaf can stay, but the summary should say the term is undefined.

## Law (verbatim)

9 CCR 2503-5, ruleVersionId 12428 (effective March 2, 2026), https://www.sos.state.co.us/CCR/GenerateRulePdf.do?fileName=9+CCR+2503-5&ruleVersionId=12428, 3.534, PDF pages 77-78:

> A. To determine the amount of income to deem to a client from a the client's spouse who does not meet the criteria described below in 'C', calculate the countable earned income of the spouse as follows: 1. Deduct $65 from the client's spouse's gross earned income; and, 2. Divide the remainder by two (2); and, 3. The result is the amount of earned income deemed to the client. 4. The deemed earned income shall be considered income to the client and shall be deducted, together with any other income, from the grant of the client. 5. Wages being garnished by the court are countable earned income.
>
> B. To determine the amount of unearned income to deem to a client from the client's spouse who does not meet the criteria as described below in 'C', calculate the countable unearned income of the spouse as follows: 1. Calculate the total amount of unearned income of the spouse; 2. Deduct the OAP grant standard from the total unearned income of the spouse; 3. Deduct an amount to meet the needs of each dependent child living in the household of the spouse equal to half the maximum SSI grant benefit standard, as defined in Section 3.510, less the dependent child's own income; 4. Deduct any medical care payments by the spouse for his or her dependents who are not covered by Medicare, Medicaid, or other health programs; 5. Deduct any amount of obligation of the spouse due to orders of judgment or for support by a court, unless there is a garnishment. Income garnished by the court is countable as unearned income. 6. The remainder is the amount of unearned income deemed to the client. 7. The deemed unearned income shall be considered income to the client and shall be deducted, together with any other income, from the grant of the client.
>
> C. If a client's spouse is receiving Adult Financial grant payments, SSI benefits, or Medicaid assistance and has income no greater than the OAP limit, his or her income shall not be considered as available to the client and shall not be deemed. If a client's spouse is institutionalized and the client has retained the minimum monthly maintenance needs allowance (MMMNA), the MMMNA shall be deducted from the institutionalized spouse's total income.

3.510, PDF page 9: "SSI benefit standard" means the maximum monthly Federal amount for an SSI recipient as listed in 20 C.F.R. 416.405-415.

## Why this is not a PR

Content must come from the signed encoder (`targeted-signed-reencode.yml`). Hand-written RuleSpec is rejected. A signed run is OpenAI-billed, and each one needs Max's approval, so this is queued rather than dispatched. Sponsor deeming (3.534(D)) can stay deferred.

## Required outputs

1. `spouse_deemed_earned_income`: `max(0, spouse gross earned − 65) / 2` when the spouse is not exempt under (C), else 0.
2. `spouse_deemed_unearned_income`: when the spouse is not exempt, `max(0, spouse total unearned − OAP grant standard (3.530(A)) − Σ over dependent children in the spouse's household of max(0, SSI benefit standard / 2 − child's own income) − spouse's medical payments for uninsured dependents − court-ordered obligations not garnished)`; else 0.
3. `oap_client_total_countable_income_with_deemed_income`: the 3.533 total (SSI included) plus deemed earned and unearned income. This is the income 3.532(B) and 3.533(B) deduct from the grant standard.
4. `effective_from: '2020-03-01'` for the 3.534 text. Pre-March-2020 versions, if encoded, follow 3.534 [Eff. 3/2/14] (ruleVersionId 8443).

## review_finding (paste)

> 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534 defers spousal unearned-income deeming (deferred output spouse_deemed_unearned_income, "requires the SSI benefit standard defined in uncopied section 3.510"), lets spouse_deemed_earned_income go negative ((earned − 65) / 2 with no floor), and never adds deemed income to the client's total countable income. Encode 3.534(B): deemed unearned = max(0, spouse unearned − OAP grant standard − Σ dependent children in the spouse's household max(0, SSI benefit standard / 2 − child's income) − medical payments for uninsured dependents − court-ordered support not garnished), taking the 3.510 SSI benefit standard ($994/month in 2026) as an input or parameter; floor deemed earnings at 0; and output the client's total countable income = 3.533 total (SSI included) + deemed earned + deemed unearned, per 3.534(A)(4) and (B)(7). Nothing is deemed from a spouse who receives Adult Financial grant payments, SSI or Medicaid with income no greater than the OAP limit (3.534(C)); the limit is undefined in the rule. The 3.534 text took effect 2020-03-01 (ruleVersionId 8577); set effective_from accordingly, not 2016-10-01 (the prior 3.534 [Eff. 3/2/14] deemed from a "non-recipient spouse" with no SSI or Medicaid exemption).

## Companion tests (2026-01; expectations from the rule text, the same ground truth as the PolicyEngine YAML in #10176)

| A. Working spouse, no assistance | earns 1,500 | no | 717.50 | 0 | Case 1 |
| B. Same spouse on Medicaid | earns 1,500; own countable (1,500 − 65 − 10) / 2 = 712.50 ≤ 1,032 | yes | 0 | 0 | Case 2 |
| C. Pension | pension 1,500 | no | 0 | 468 | Case 3 |
| D. Pension and child support | pension 1,500; court-ordered child support 200 | no | 0 | 268 | Case 4 |
| E. Dependent child, no income | pension 2,000; one child, no income | no | 0 | 471 | Case 5 |
| F. Dependent child with income | pension 2,000; one child with 100 income | no | 0 | 571 | Case 6 |
| G. Spouse on SSI within the limit | earns 1,000; SSI 536.50; own total 1,004 ≤ 1,032 | yes | 0 | 0 | Case 7 |
| H. Earnings under $65 | earns 50 | no | 0 | 0 | Case 8 |
| I. Earned and unearned | earns 1,000; pension 1,200 | no | 467.50 | 168 | Case 10 |

items.body:
## Encoding debt

New Jersey's federally administered Optional State Supplementation (OSS) has no RuleSpec module. On `rulespec-us` `main` (`172bf04e4`, 2026-10-14), `us-nj/` holds only:

- `policies/cms/` (CHIP and Medicaid eligibility levels)
- `policies/income_tax/`
- `regulations/njac-10-90/` (WorkFirst New Jersey)
- `statutes/54a:4-7` (the New Jersey earned income tax credit)

There is no `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/` tree like the DC and Delaware ones, and no SSI module under `us-nj/statutes/`. The shared module `us/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/federally-administered-optional-supplement-common.yaml` already holds the 2026 federal amounts New Jersey's tables use: FBR 994.00 and 1,491.00 (`federal_code_a_individual_fbr`, `federal_code_a_couple_fbr`), the federal code C individual FBR 994.00, FBR less VTR 662.67 and 994.00, the Title XIX caps 30.00 and 60.00, and the code Y waiver (`optional_supplement_waived_os_code_applies`). No module encodes the federal OSS computation in 20 CFR 416.2025, and there is no `us/regulations/20-cfr/` tree.

Issue searches for "New Jersey supplementary", "New Jersey SSP", "New Jersey state supplement", "New Jersey optional", "New Jersey SSI", "44:7-86", "01415.058", "NY01415.025", "nj_ssp" and "us-nj" SSP find no issue for this program. "01415.058" finds #1450 and #1767 and the closed DC and Delaware issues #519, #520 and #532; "New Jersey SSI" finds only #1481 (New Jersey LIHEAP). The SSP `pe-parity` issues cover California (#1450), New Mexico (#1708), Texas (#1709), Wyoming (#1766), Nevada (#1767) and New Hampshire (#1769).

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10157 (open, not merged) adds the program to PolicyEngine-US:

- **Variables** (Person, monthly), under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nj/njdhs/ssp/`:
  - `nj_ssp_care_setting`, an input: `CONGREGATE_CARE`, `RESIDENTIAL_HEALTH_CARE`, `EXCLUDED` (publicly operated community residences, emergency shelters, and institutionalized children whose care private insurance pays) or `NONE`.
  - `nj_ssp_living_arrangement`, the OS code: `CONGREGATE_CARE` (A), `LIVING_ALONE_OR_WITH_OTHERS` (B), `LIVING_ONLY_WITH_INELIGIBLE_SPOUSE` (C), `HOUSEHOLD_OF_ANOTHER` (D), `RESIDENTIAL_HEALTH_CARE` (I), `MEDICAID_INSTITUTION` (G) or `NONE` (Z). It reads the care setting, the federal living arrangement, the medical-facility input, `is_ssi_ineligible_spouse`, and whether anyone outside the marital unit lives in the household. It can also be set directly.
  - `nj_ssp`, the payment. It calls the shared helper `ssi_state_supplement` (`policyengine_us/variables/gov/ssa/ssi/_ssi_state_supplement.py`, which PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10001 also adds). The helper computes the level before income internally; no output variable holds that level.
- **Parameters,** dated 2026-01-01:
  - `gov.states.nj.njdhs.ssp.amount.individual` and `.couple`, broken down by `nj_ssp_living_arrangement`. The couple file's code C cell is a 25.35 placeholder (see "Interpretations and gaps").
  - The federal `gov.ssa.ssi.state_supplement.minimum_payment`, $1.
- **Tests** under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/nj/njdhs/ssp/`: `nj_ssp.yaml` (17 cases), `nj_ssp_living_arrangement.yaml` (11) and `integration.yaml` (9), 37 in total.
- **Aggregates:** `nj_ssp` is added to `household_state_benefits`, `spm_unit_benefits`, SNAP unearned income and HUD unearned income.
- **Scope:** 2026 only. Earlier years and mandatory (grandfathered) supplementation are out of scope; the registry status is `partial`.
- **Changes after the first review:**
  - The files moved from `nj/dhs/ssp` to `nj/njdhs/ssp`, so the parameters are now `gov.states.nj.njdhs.ssp.*`.
  - `integration.yaml` Cases 2 and 6 were renamed and given comments; their inputs are unchanged. Case 2 now describes a congregate care couple in a small household-scale facility; no input holds the facility's size or institution status. Case 6 now describes a couple living only with a foster child; the child is a 12-year-old tax-unit dependent with no foster-care input, and code C is entered directly. Case 7 also checks `spm_unit_benefits`, and Case 8 (congregate care spouses paid as individuals after the month of entry) and Case 9 (code B under deeming, with a spouse earning $34,590 a year and a 12-year-old) are new.
  - `nj_ssp.yaml` Case 17 (a disabled child living with parents) is new.

## Module paths and corpus citations

| Proposed module | Provisions | Corpus citation | Corpus status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/nj-ssp-living-arrangement-variations.yaml` | OS codes A, B, C, D, I, G and Z and the Lifeline NOTE (SI 01415.058 J.1). Code Y comes from the shared module | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058/block-34` | In axiom-corpus manifest `manifests/us-ssa-poms-si-2026-09-10.yaml`: source id `ssa-poms-si-01415-058` (TN 95, expression date 2026-08-28) |
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/nj-ssp-individual-state-supplement-levels.yaml` | J.2.a, all 9 rows and both footnotes | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058/block-35` and `block-36` | Same manifest |
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/nj-ssp-couple-state-supplement-levels.yaml` | J.2.b, all 6 rows and footnotes 1 to 3 | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058/block-35` and `block-37` | Same manifest |
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-ny01415-025/nj-oss-codes.yaml` | SI NY01415.025: code C (the household rule, the separate-household and foster-child exceptions, transients); the NOTE under codes A and I (couple status after entry into a facility); code Z's privately insured children | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/ny01415.025/block-2` | Same manifest: source id `ssa-poms-si-ny01415-025` (expression date 2022-09-13). The New Jersey row of `manifests/ssi-agent-queue.yaml` (`agent_ready`) names this section and SI 01415.058 J |
| `us-nj/statutes/44:7-86.yaml` (the `us-nj/statutes/54a:4-7.yaml` path style) | N.J.S.A. 44:7-86, which SSA gives as New Jersey's "Statutory basis for payment" | none | Not in any `us-nj` manifest or corpus lock on `main`; needs ingest from the New Jersey Legislature's statutes database (`lis.njleg.state.nj.us`, the source of `us-nj/statutes/54a:4-7`). I couldn't retrieve the section, so this issue doesn't quote it |
| Co-cited source | SSA, State Assistance Programs for SSI Recipients, January 2011, New Jersey: SSA administration, the statutory basis and the scope of coverage | none | Not ingested. `manifests/us-ssa-w6-federal-guidance.yaml` holds other states' 2011 pages (for example `us/guidance/ssa/state-assistance-programs-for-ssi-recipients/2011/de`) but not New Jersey's; needs ingest: https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/progdesc/ssi_st_asst/2011/nj.html |
| `us-nj/policies/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026/nj-ssp-payment.yaml` | Federal administration (SI 01415.058 A; SI NY01415.025 A). The federal computation: 20 CFR 416.2025(b) and 416.2020(c); SI 02001.005 A.2 and B.2; SI 02001.010 A.1 to A.3; SI 02005.030 A.1 and G; SI 01320.430 C.5, C.7, D and example G.4 | `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01415.058/block-1`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/ny01415.025/block-1`; `us/regulation/20/416/2025`; `us/regulation/20/416/2020`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/02001.005/block-2` and `block-7`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/02001.010/block-1` to `block-3`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/02005.030/block-1`, `block-14` and `block-15`; `us/manual/ssa/poms/si/01320.430/block-7`, `block-9`, `block-11` to `block-13` and `block-35` | The POMS sections are in `manifests/us-ssa-poms-si-2026-09-10.yaml`. 20 CFR 416.2020 and 416.2025 are not listed in a `manifests/*.yaml` document file. Part 416 is the eCFR extraction scope `us/regulation/2026-09-11-title-20-part-416` (row in `manifests/ssi-agent-queue.yaml`; corpus lock `.axiom/corpus-locks/us/regulation/2026-09-11-title-20-part-416.json`); its provisions are section-level, with no blocks |

- **Block numbers.** I took them from the provisions JSONL git blobs named in the corpus locks on `main`: `831feb4ce2` (`data/corpus/provisions/us/manual/2026-09-10-ssi-poms-si.jsonl`) and `9fa9a51e6f` (`data/corpus/provisions/us/regulation/2026-09-11-title-20-part-416.jsonl`). Both downloads match the sha256 in their lock. Blocks 34, 36 and 37 of SI 01415.058 and block 2 of SI NY01415.025 match the live pages word for word, apart from spacing and footnote markers.
- **Second copy of SI 01415.058.** The DC run also holds the section as `us/guidance/ssa/poms/si-01415-058/2026` (TN 94, `manifests/us-dc-ossp-ssa-poms.yaml`, `source_as_of` 2025-12-09); the shared module cites that copy. Its New Jersey subsection is `block-35` to `block-38`. Its two tables are identical to blocks 36 and 37 above. Its J.1 text differs only in quotation marks (for example OS code "A" and a separate "household") and one apostrophe ("Department of Human Services' Division"). The New Jersey row of `manifests/ssi-agent-queue.yaml` names the manual-family paths used above.
- **The payment module.** As in #1767, the last module holds federal rules that every federally administered state shares. If #1767's encoder builds a shared module instead (for example `us/regulations/20-cfr/416/2025.yaml`), the New Jersey module should import it. The outputs and tests below don't change either way.

I checked presence in the manifests on axiom-corpus `main` (`437198d6c`). I did not check the signed release that rulespec-us pins.

## Source text (verbatim)

**POMS SI 01415.058, Federally Administered Optional Supplementary Payment Programs for January 2026** (TN 95, "Effective Dates: 08/28/2026 - Present"), https://secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0501415058

Subsection A:

> The following states participate in federally administered optional supplementary payment programs:

The table that follows lists "New Jersey" with the reference "SI 01415.058J".

Subsection J.1, "Definitions of State living arrangement variations for New Jersey":

> **A** Congregate care
> Apply OS code A to recipients in Federal living arrangement A. The living arrangement includes:
> • recipients in residential facilities who are under the supervision of the Department of Human Services;
> • children and adults in residential facilities (both inside and outside of NJ) who are under the supervision of, or placed by the NJ Department of Human Services Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) or Division of Youth and Family Services (DYFS); and
> • recipients living in assisted living residences or comprehensive personal care homes (CPCH) licensed by the Department of Health and Senior Services.
>
> **B** Living alone or with others
> Use OS code B for recipients whose Federal living arrangements are A or C and who do not meet the requirements defined in other supplementation categories.
> You must consider any eligible recipient who meets the requirement for a Federal code A to be in optional supplement B unless they are residing in a residential health care facility or living alone with an ineligible spouse.
> Likewise, any child meeting the criteria for a Federal code C is automatically entitled to optional supplement B.
> This category includes, but is not limited to, recipients who are in one of the following situations:
> 1. Living physically alone;
> 2. Living with others in a private dwelling, but meet some criteria for Federal living arrangement A; or
> 3. Placed in a transitional residency program by the Division of Mental Health and Hospitals, Department of Human Services.
> Optional supplement code B is the proper code to use with an intervening Federal code A. For State supplement codes, see SM 01301.535.
> Use OS code B to address Section 1619 cases.
>
> **C** Living alone with an ineligible spouse
> Use OS code C when a recipient lives with ONLY their ineligible spouse and NO other persons are part of the household. Use Federal criteria to determine an ineligible spouse for State supplementation purposes (i.e., a spouse, either by marriage or holding out as spouses) who is either not eligible for SSI or who chooses not to apply. If other persons, even minor children, are present in the household, you cannot apply this OS code.
> It is possible that a claimant and the ineligible spouse live with others and allege that they are a separate household by virtue of the fact that they eat their meals out or have separate purchase and preparation of food. In this instance, you may consider an optional supplement C as long as no other person is considered part of the household. There is no couple counterpart in this category.
> A transient recipient who co-exists only with an ineligible spouse also qualifies as OS code C.
> Always consider parent(s) with minor children to be in the same household and code the case OS code B.
>
> **D** Living in the household of another
> Apply OS code D to recipients who are living in the household of another for Federal purposes.
>
> **I** Licensed residential health care facilities (RHCF)
> Apply OS code I to recipients living in:
> • attached nursing homes;
> • assisted living residence;
> • CPCH; or
> • free-standing licensed residential health care facilities. We paid residents of these facilities the OS A rate prior to January 1, 2006.
> We must base our authorization for this payment on the recipient's verified residence at a facility listed in the New Jersey Congregate Care Directory.
> Only the RHCF section of a multipurpose facility is eligible for the OS code I rate. Pay residents of the assisted living resident (ALR or CPCH section of a multipurpose facility) at the OS code A rate. Nursing home residents are in living arrangement (D or G) if Medicaid pays more than 50 percent of the cost of care.
>
> **G** Apply OS code G effective September 1, 1988, when the State elected Federal administration of an optional State supplementary payment to residents of Title XIX facilities.
>
> **Z** No supplement cases
> Apply OS code Z to recipients:
> • in licensed medical facilities where Medicaid is paying less than 50 percent of the cost of care;
> • in publicly operated community residences having 16 or less residents; and
> • residing throughout a month in publicly operated emergency shelters.
> You can also apply OS code Z to cases that were FLA D prior to January 1988, or effective December 1, 1996, to children residing in public or private facilities where private health insurance paid for their care. For determination of applicability of $30 payment limit, see SI 00520.011.
>
> NOTE: All State Supplement payments, except for medicaid facilities, include a Lifeline payment which is a utility assistance program for older people and people with disabilities that offers an annual benefit amount for individuals who receive SSI.

The code letters in bold are the table's Code column. Code G's cell has no title. Code Y ("Optional supplementation waived") sits between G and Z and is omitted here; the shared module encodes it.

Subsection J.2:

> The following charts display the coding and monthly payments levels for New Jersey effective January 1, 2026:

"a. Recipient payment levels for New Jersey". Blank cells continue the code above them, as in the source's merged cells.

| Federal Code | State OS Code | Category | FBR | State Supplement Level | Total Payment Levels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | A | All | 994.00 | 150.05 | 1144.05 |
| | B | All | 994.00 | 31.25 | 1025.25 |
| | C | Individual | 994.00 | 152.99 | 1146.99 |
| | I | All | 994.00 | 210.05 | 1204.05 |
| | Z | All | 994.00 | 0.00 | 994.00 |
| B | D | All | 662.67<sup>1</sup> | 44.31 | 706.98 |
| C | B | All | 994.00 | 31.25 | 1025.25 |
| D | G | All | 30.00<sup>2</sup> | 20.00 | 50.00 |
| | Z | All | 30.00 | 0.00 | 30.00 |

> <sup>1</sup>Not the FBR; the amount represents the FBR less VTR.
> <sup>2</sup>Not the FBR; the amount represents a payment cap to recipients in a Title XIX institution.

"b. Couple payment levels for New Jersey":

| Federal Code | State OS Code | Category | FBR | State Supplement Level | Total Payment Levels |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | A | All | 1491.00 | 618.35 | 2109.35<sup>1</sup> |
| | B | All | 1491.00 | 25.35 | 1516.35<sup>1</sup> |
| | I | All | 1491.00 | 738.35 | 2229.35<sup>1</sup> |
| | Z | All | 1491.00 | 0.00 | 1491.00 |
| B | D | All | 994.00<sup>2</sup> | 93.08 | 1087.08<sup>1</sup> |
| D | G | All | 60.00<sup>3</sup> | 40.00 | 100.00 |

> <sup>1</sup>This amount is the total of the federal payment, the state supplement amount, and the lifeline payment. When added together and divided in half for each member of the couple, the result includes a half penny. The total is rounded up to accommodate system processing.
> <sup>2</sup>Not the FBR; the amount represents the FBR less VTR.
> <sup>3</sup>Not the FBR; the amount represents a payment cap to recipients in a Title XIX institution.

**POMS SI NY01415.025, New Jersey Payments (RTS 398 - 06/2006)** ("Effective Dates: 09/13/2022 - Present"), https://secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0501415025NY

A, "Introduction":

> Since the beginning of the SSI Program, SSA has administered Optional State Supplement (OSS) payments on behalf of New Jersey.

B, "OSS Codes", code C:

> **C** Living Alone with an Ineligible Spouse
> Used when an individual lives with the individual's ineligible spouse and there are no other persons who are part of the household. An ineligible spouse for State supplementation purposes is determined by using Federal criteria, i.e., a spouse, either by marriage or holding out who is either ineligible for SSI or who chooses not to apply.
> Once other persons, even minor children, are present in the household, this supplementary payment variation cannot exist. However, it is possible that a claimant and the claimant's ineligible spouse live with others and allege that they are a separate "household" by virtue of the fact that they eat their meals out or have separate purchase and preparation of food. In this instance, an OSS C is permissible as long as no other person is in their household. There is no couple counterpart in this category. The state determination of eating all meals out or separate purchase and preparation of food must be documented on the Optional State Supplement page.
> A transient individual who co-exists only with an ineligible spouse will also qualify for the OSS C rate.
> An individual living alone only with an ineligible spouse and foster child(ren) will also qualify for the OSS C rate (effective 7/1/90).

The same NOTE closes the code A and code I cells:

> NOTE - When a couple enters a Level 2 facility, they will usually get the couple FBR and couple OSS D for the month of change only. After that, they are treated as two individuals, since couple status can exist only in households, not institutions, per SI 00501.154. However, while Level 2 facilities usually meet the Federal definition of institution, this is not always the case (e.g., facility serves fewer than four people). In such small scale "household" (i.e., non-institutional) Level 2 facilities, couple status can continue.

Code Z, last sentence:

> It also includes cases that were FLA D prior to January 1988 or effective 12/1/96 children under age 18 residing in certain public or private facilities receiving payment for their care under any health insurance policy issued by a private provider (SI 00520.011).

**SSA, State Assistance Programs for SSI Recipients, January 2011, New Jersey,** https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/progdesc/ssi_st_asst/2011/nj.html (read through the Wayback Machine's raw copy; www.ssa.gov refuses scripted requests)

> Mandatory Minimum Supplementation
> Administration: Social Security Administration.
> Optional State Supplementation
> Administration: Social Security Administration.
> Effective date: January 1, 1974.
> Statutory basis for payment: New Jersey Statutes Annotated, 44:7-86.

> Scope of coverage: Optional state supplement provided to all aged, blind, and disabled recipients, including children, except those in publicly operated community residences or facilities where Medicaid pays less than 50 percent of the cost of care. Supplementation provided to recipients in approved residential facilities.

**POMS SI 01320.430, Effect of Spouse-to-Spouse Deeming on Optional State Supplementation** (TN 60, "Effective Dates: 12/02/2024 - Present"), https://secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0501320430

C.7, "OSS Payment Category for Ineligible Spouse", with its NOTE:

> Effective October 1, 1988, to determine the OSS for a couple, the ineligible spouse is considered to be in the same category (i.e., aged, blind or disabled) as the eligible individual. (Currently, four States vary their payment rates by category: California, Iowa, Massachusetts, and Nevada.) The State supplement rate used is the greater of: • The eligible couple rate for the category for which the eligible individual qualifies; or • the eligible individual rate (including the special rate for an eligible individual living with an ineligible spouse) for the category for which the eligible individual qualifies.
> NOTE: Currently, only the States of New Jersey and Washington have a higher OSS rate for an eligible individual than for an eligible couple.

D.1, "Determine Eligibility/Payment as an Individual":

> a. Subtract the eligible individual's own countable income from the FBR for an individual. The remainder is the Federal benefit as an individual, or excess countable income.
> b. If a Federal Benefit is due under a. above, use the full OSS for an individual, or the OSS for an individual with an ineligible spouse, in those States which provide such an OSS.
> c. If there is excess countable income remaining in a. above, subtract the excess from the OSS for an individual. The remainder is the State supplement due as an individual. (If no Federal or State benefit is due, deeming is not applicable.)

D.2, "Follow Spouse-to-Spouse Deeming Rules" (a., second sentence; b. to d.):

> If the ineligible spouse's total income after allocations is more than the difference between the FBR for an eligible couple and the FBR for an eligible individual, combine the eligible individual's and ineligible spouse's incomes and treat as an eligible couple.
> b. Subtract the couple's countable income (after applying appropriate exclusions and allowances) from the FBR for a couple. The remainder is the Federal benefit due a couple using the deeming rules. Where the couple's countable income is greater, excess countable income results, and no Federal benefit is payable.
> c. If a Federal benefit is due based on use of the ineligible spouse's income, the State supplement used is the full OSS for a couple who are both aged, both blind, or both disabled (depending on the category of the eligible individual's SSI benefit).
> If the State provides different payment variations, select the variation that applies to the eligible individual, and use the corresponding OSS for a couple.
> However, if the State has an individual supplement rate (including a special rate for an eligible individual living with an ineligible spouse) which is greater than the State supplement for an eligible couple, use the higher individual State supplement.
> d. If there is excess countable income remaining in step 2.b., subtract the excess from the OSS for a couple (or the individual State supplement, if greater). The remainder is the State supplement due a couple using the deeming rules. (If no Federal or State benefit is due, the individual is ineligible due to excess income.)

D.3, "Determine Federal Benefit/State Supplement Amounts":

> a. The Federal benefit amount is the lesser of: • The Federal benefit due as an individual (step 1.a.); or • The Federal benefit due using the deeming rules (step 2.b.).
> b. The State supplement amount is the lesser of: • The State supplement due as an individual (step 1.b. or c.); or • The State supplement due using the deeming rules (step 2.c. or d.).

Example G.4.c (Washington, whose special rate for an individual with an ineligible spouse exceeds its couple rate):

> We must first determine which OSS rate to use in the couple's computation, since this particular State has a special individual rate for an eligible individual with an ineligible spouse which is higher than the rate for a couple. After using that figure in the couple computation, the result is still compared to the OSS due in the individual computation; the lower amount is the actual benefit due.

> (b) Effect of countable income on payment amounts. Countable income of an eligible individual or eligible couple is determined in the same manner as such income is determined under the title XVI supplemental security income program. Countable income will affect the amount of the State supplementary payments as follows:
> (1) As provided in § 416.420, countable income will first be deducted from the Federal benefit rate applicable to an eligible individual or eligible couple. The monthly payment formula:

- **Individual:** `max(0, level − max(0, countable income − FBR))`. The FBR is 994.00 for federal codes A and C, 662.67 for code B and the 30.00 payment cap for code D (416.2025(b)(2)-(4); J.2.a).
- **Eligible couple living together:** the same formula on the couple's combined countable income, the couple FBR (1,491.00; 994.00 for code B; 60.00 for code D) and the J.2.b level. The result is divided by 2 (SI 02005.030 G.1).
- **Eligible individual with deemed income from an ineligible spouse:** the lesser of two amounts (SI 01320.430 D.3.b; 416.2025(b)(3)):
  - the individual computation, with the person's own countable income and the individual FBR, using the code C level when code C applies (D.1.a-c);
  - the couple computation, with the couple's countable income, the couple FBR, and the higher of the couple level for the person's variation and the individual level (C.7, D.2.b-d).
  - In New Jersey the individual level is the higher one for code B (31.25 against 25.35) and code C (152.99; no couple level). The couple level is higher for codes A, I, D and G.
- **Rounding:** each person's amount is raised to the next cent using the third decimal digit only (SI 02001.010 A.1-A.3). Halving the A, B and I couple levels leaves a half cent, so each member gets 309.18, 12.68 or 369.18 (J.2.b footnote 1).
- **Minimum:** a positive amount below $1 is paid as $1.00, per member for a couple (416.2020(c); SI 02001.005 A.2, B.2).

Inputs: State of residence; SSI category facts (aged, blind, disabled; age); SSI eligibility for the month apart from income (resources, immigration status, residence); federal living arrangement (A, B, C or D); facility facts (a facility listed in the Congregate Care Directory and which section; a licensed medical facility and Medicaid's share of the cost of care; a publicly operated community residence and its size; a full month in a publicly operated emergency shelter; a child whose facility care private insurance pays; federal code D before January 1988); marital or holding-out status, living together, and whether the spouse is eligible for SSI or chooses not to apply; whether anyone other than the spouse and foster children is part of the household; the State's separate-household determination; transient status; waiver of the supplement; the month of entry into a facility and whether the facility is an institution; whether ineligible-spouse deeming applies; monthly countable income under the federal SSI rules (own, couple, or with deemed income).

## Interpretations and gaps

- **Code C has no couple level.** J.1 says "There is no couple counterpart in this category", and J.2.b has no C row.
  - PolicyEngine-US's `couple.yaml` holds 25.35 (the B couple level) for `LIVING_ONLY_WITH_INELIGIBLE_SPOUSE`, with a comment that it never affects results. A code C claimant is never part of an eligible couple, and under deeming the helper uses `max(couple, individual)` = 152.99 (Case L).
  - The encoding should leave the C couple cell undefined and use the individual level in the deeming computation directly (D.2.c, "use the higher individual State supplement"). A parity check should skip that parameter cell.
- **The code C household test.** PolicyEngine-US gives code C when the person's marital unit holds an SSI-ineligible spouse and nobody outside the marital unit lives in the household.
  - Neither exception can be derived: foster children (SI NY01415.025, effective 7/1/90) and the separate household for couples who eat out or buy and prepare food separately. Both go through an explicit `nj_ssp_living_arrangement` input (the variable's documentation says so). Transients are covered when the household holds only the couple.
  - `integration.yaml` Case 6 enters code C directly for a couple living only with a foster child (12) and pays 152.99. It is the PolicyEngine-US case for the foster-child exception through the explicit input.
  - The encoding should take "other persons in the household, excluding foster children" and the State's separate-household determination as inputs.
- **A spouse who chooses not to apply.** J.1 counts a spouse "who is either not eligible for SSI or who chooses not to apply" as an ineligible spouse; SI NY01415.025 says "who is either ineligible for SSI or who chooses not to apply".
  - PolicyEngine-US's `is_ssi_ineligible_spouse` covers only a spouse who is not aged, blind or disabled, and `ssi_claim_is_joint` ignores take-up. So when one aged spouse doesn't apply, the couple is computed jointly and the applicant gets half the B couple level (12.68) instead of the C level (152.99, subject to deeming). An aged, blind or disabled spouse who is ineligible for another reason is treated the same way.
  - A NOTE in `nj_ssp.py` documents this. No PolicyEngine-US case covers it. The encoding should follow J.1.
- **Couples in a facility.** The SI NY01415.025 NOTE gives a couple entering a Level 2 facility "the couple FBR and couple OSS D for the month of change only"; after that, the spouses are two individuals, except in a small-scale facility that is not an institution.
  - PolicyEngine-US has no month-of-change or institution input, so it computes congregate care spouses in one marital unit jointly. `integration.yaml` Case 8 enters congregate care spouses as separate marital units to pay 150.05 each (Case K).
  - `integration.yaml` Case 2 pays the A couple level (309.18 each) in a small household-scale facility where couple status continues (Case J).
  - The month of entry itself has no PolicyEngine-US case and is not modelled. Read literally, the NOTE names "couple OSS D" (93.08 in J.2.b, a federal code B row) for that month, although J.2.b prints A and I couple levels under federal code A. The encoding should record which reading it takes for the month of entry.
  - The helper averages the two members' couple levels when spouses in one marital unit have different codes (NOTE in `nj_ssp.py`). SI 02005.030 G.1 says to "average their individual OSS payment" for multi-living-arrangement couples living together. No New Jersey case covers a mixed couple.
- **Code B under deeming.** The B individual level exceeds the B couple level (31.25 against 25.35); the C.7 NOTE names New Jersey and Washington. Code B with an ineligible spouse arises when someone else is in the household, such as a child.
  - Under deeming, the couple computation uses 31.25 (D.2.c) instead of the 25.35 couple level: the full 31.25 when the couple's countable income after the child's allocation is at or below 1,491, and 31.25 less the excess when it is above 1,491 (D.2.d), reaching $0 at 1,522.25. The payment is the lesser of that and the individual computation (D.3.b), so this reading pays 31.25 rather than 25.35 whenever own countable income is at most 994 and couple countable income is at most 1,491. PolicyEngine-US follows this reading. `integration.yaml` Case 9 (an aged recipient, a spouse earning $34,590 a year and a 12-year-old) has couple countable income of 1,150.25 and pays 31.25; no companion test covers it.

> 2. Judgments for the month:
>    - Code Z: in a licensed medical facility where Medicaid pays less than 50 percent of the cost, OR in a publicly operated community residence with 16 or fewer residents, OR in a publicly operated emergency shelter throughout the month, OR a child under 18 in a facility whose care private health insurance pays (from December 1, 1996), OR a case that was federal code D before January 1988.
>    - Code G: federal living arrangement D (Title XIX facility, Medicaid pays more than 50 percent), and not code Z.
>    - Code C: lives with an ineligible spouse (federal criteria: married or holding out, and not eligible for SSI or choosing not to apply) AND no other person is part of the household, where foster children don't count and a documented State determination of eating out or separate purchase and preparation of food makes the claimant and spouse a separate household. Never when parents live with minor children.
> 3. The OS code for the month: Z or G as above; Y if waived; otherwise A in a congregate care setting (a residential facility supervised by the Department of Human Services, a DDD or DCF placement, or an assisted living residence or comprehensive personal care home in the New Jersey Congregate Care Directory), I in the RHCF section of a licensed residential health care facility in the Directory, D in federal living arrangement B, C as above, and B for anyone else in federal living arrangement A or C.
> 4. A Money output, the monthly payment for each person:
>    - max(0, level − max(0, countable income − FBR)), zero when countable income is at or above FBR + level (416.2025(b)(2)-(4)).
>    - An eligible couple living together is computed jointly with the couple FBR and the J.2.b level, and the result is divided by 2 (SI 02005.030 G.1). Spouses in an institution are two individuals after the month of change unless the facility is a small-scale household (SI NY01415.025 NOTE).

>    - Each person's amount is raised to the next cent using the third decimal only (SI 02001.010 A.1-A.3). A positive amount below $1 is paid as $1.00, per member for a couple (416.2020(c); SI 02001.005 A.2, B.2).
>
> Companion tests, each assigning every leaf input: cases A to R in the issue's Companion tests table.

- `nj_ssp_living_arrangement` (the OS code; codes Z, G and C are its `NONE`, `MEDICAID_INSTITUTION` and `LIVING_ONLY_WITH_INELIGIBLE_SPOUSE` values);
- `nj_ssp` (the payment; no output variable holds the per-person level);

## Encoding debt

North Carolina's State-County Special Assistance (SA) has no RuleSpec module. It is a state-administered SSI supplement for adult care homes (basic rate), special care units (enhanced rate) and SA In-Home (SAIH). On `rulespec-us` `main` (`d8511cca7`, 2026-10-15), `us-nc/statutes/` holds only `105/`, `us-nc/regulations/10a-ncac/` only `71u/`, and `us-nc/policies/dhhs/` only `fns/`. Searches for "Special Assistance", "State-County Special Assistance", "108A-41", "108A-42.1" and "North Carolina SSP" find no SA issue. #1466 (North Carolina LIEAP) is related: SA counts as unearned income there (SAIH Manual SA-5400 II; FNS 300.02).

PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10160 (merged) adds the program to PolicyEngine-US; PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10288 adds the 2027 rates:

- **Variables** under `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nc/ncdhhs/sa/`, all Person and monthly: `nc_sa`, `nc_sa_eligible`, `nc_sa_full_month_amount`, `nc_sa_rate`, `nc_sa_countable_income` and `nc_sa_countable_for_hud`. The inputs are `nc_sa_care_setting`, `nc_sa_facility_rate` (0 means the published rate) and `nc_sa_partial_month_days` (0 means a full month).
- **Parameters** under `gov.states.nc.ncdhhs.sa`: `rate.basic` and `rate.enhanced` (2026 and 2027 values; later years are projected with `gov.ssa.uprating` and rounded to $1 until SSA announces each COLA), `personal_needs_allowance` and `minimum_adult_age`. The $2,000 resource limit and the $20, $65 and one-half exclusions reuse SSI's parameters (SA-3100 II.C).
- **Tests** under `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/nc/ncdhhs/sa/`: `nc_sa.yaml` (39 cases), `integration.yaml` (9), `nc_sa_eligible.yaml` (9), `nc_sa_rate.yaml` (7), `nc_sa_countable_for_hud.yaml` (6) and `nc_sa_countable_income.yaml` (5).
- **Scope:** 2026 rates from 2026-01-01 and 2027 rates from 2027-01-01. Earlier years are out of scope, as are open/shut payments, Basic-to-SCU supplements and the first two months of a one-third-reduced SSI.

## Module paths and corpus citations

| Proposed module | Provisions | Corpus status |

| `us-nc/statutes/108a/108a-41.yaml` | (b)(1) categories, (b)(2) income limits | Needs ingest: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/PDF/BySection/Chapter_108A/GS_108A-41.pdf#page=1. The corpus has only `us-nc/statute/chapter-108a/108a-27-01` from Chapter 108A |
| `us-nc/statutes/108a/108a-42.1.yaml` | (a)-(b) rates and COLA indexing | Needs ingest: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/PDF/BySection/Chapter_108A/GS_108A-42.1.pdf |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/special-assistance-manual/sa-3100-eligibility.yaml` (if needed) | I, II.A-C, III.C | In the corpus as `us-nc/manual/dss/special-assistance/manual` (manifest `manifests/us-nc-ssi-state-supplement.yaml`, revised June 1, 2026), pp. 6-10 |
| `.../special-assistance-manual/sa-3200-resources.yaml` | I | Same, p. 61 |
| `.../special-assistance-manual/sa-3210-income.yaml` | IV, V.A, V.B.1, V.D.1.e | Same, pp. 185-195 |
| `.../special-assistance-manual/sa-3220-budgeting-principles.yaml` | I-IV, VIII | Same, pp. 204-219 |
| `us-nc/policies/dhhs/special-assistance-in-home-manual/sa-5300-calculation-of-payments.yaml` | SA-5300 IV; co-cite SA-5400 V | In the corpus as `us-nc/manual/dss/special-assistance/in-home-manual` (same manifest), pp. 41-43, 48 |
| Co-cited: 10A NCAC 71P .0603(3) | SSI application | Needs ingest: http://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2010a%20-%20health%20and%20human%20services/chapter%2071%20-%20adult%20and%20family%20support/subchapter%20p/subchapter%20p%20rules.pdf#page=11 |
| Co-cited for the 2026 amounts | Change notice EFS-SA-CN-01-2026 | Needs ingest: https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/EFS-SA-CN-01-2026.pdf#page=1 |
| Co-cited for the 2027 COLA | SSA 2027 COLA fact sheet (3.6%; FBR $1,029) | Needs ingest: https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2027.html. NCDHHS's 2027 change notice, once published (the 2026 notice is dated January 7, 2026), replaces the derived 2027 values as the source |

I checked the manifests on axiom-corpus `main` (`2137e79be`), not the signed release that rulespec-us pins.

## Source text (verbatim)

**G.S. 108A-41(b):**

> (1) Meets one of the following: a. Is 65 years of age or older. b. Is between the ages of 18 and 65, and is permanently and totally disabled or is legally blind pursuant to G.S. 111-11.

> a. The total countable monthly income for individuals residing in adult care home facilities or in-home living arrangements without a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or dementia shall not exceed the basic rate established in subsection (a) of G.S. 108A-42.1 plus a personal needs allowance in an amount determined by the General Assembly.

(b)(2)b is the same for "special care units or in-home living arrangements with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or dementia" and the enhanced rate.

**G.S. 108A-42.1(a):**

> The maximum monthly rate for State-County Special Assistance recipients residing in adult care homes or in-home living arrangements without a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or dementia is one thousand two hundred eighty-five dollars ($1,285) per month per resident. This rate shall be adjusted on January 1, 2024, and each January 1 thereafter, using the federally approved Social Security cost-of-living adjustment effective for the applicable year.

(b) is the same for the enhanced rate, "one thousand six hundred forty-seven dollars ($1,647)".

**SA-3100 I, II.A-C** ([p. 6](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/Special-Assistance-Manual-Rev-June-2026.pdf#page=6), 7):

> To be eligible for SA, an individual must be eligible for SSI, or ineligible for SSI solely due to being over income for SSI.

> 1. Be an individual who is age 65 or older; or is 18-64 and disabled or legally blind; or an individual who is under 18 and is legally blind. [...] 5. Not be an inmate in a jail or prison. 6. Receive SSI or are financially ineligible for SSI solely due to being over income for SSI.

> A current SSI beneficiary automatically meets the categorical and financial requirements for SA.

> To receive SA, non-SSI beneficiaries must meet the eligibility requirements for SSI except for income.

**SA-3200 I** ([p. 61](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/Special-Assistance-Manual-Rev-June-2026.pdf#page=61)):

> The resource limit is $2000 for an applicant/recipient. The budget unit is always one.

> SSI recipients automatically meet the resource requirements for SA.

**SA-3210 IV, V** ([pp. 185-195](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/Special-Assistance-Manual-Rev-June-2026.pdf#page=185)):

> Subtract the $20 SA General Income Exclusion. [...] Apply the SA General Income Exclusion to unearned income first. Apply any remainder to earned income.

> Subtract the $65 Earned Income Exclusion. [...] Subtract ½ of the remaining earned income. Never reduce earned income below zero.

> 4. If the a/b currently has income at or above the FBR, a referral to SSA to apply for SSI is not required.

> b. This reason is time limited for SA Basic and SCU cases and provides for budgeting of the SA payment for not more than a two-month period following the a/b's month of admission to a SA eligible facility.

> Exceptions to SSI FBR for SA applicants: (1) Individuals who are receiving less than the FBR due to recoupment of SSI or RSDI. (2) When SSA is considering an individual as part of a married couple. (3) When SSI is one-third reduced for a private living arrangement and application is for SAIH.

**SA-3220 I-IV** ([pp. 204-210](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/Special-Assistance-Manual-Rev-June-2026.pdf#page=204)):

> NOTE: SA is always a budget unit of one. Count only the income of the SA applicant/recipient.

> The current SA Basic rate, effective January 1, 2026, is $1,397. [...] A facility may choose to offer a lower rate to SA recipients. Should this occur, the actual rate charged to the recipient, rather than the legislative established SA facility rate, is used in the calculations addressed in this chapter.

> The current Enhanced rate, effective January 1, 2026, is $1,792.

> A $70 personal needs allowance is added to the monthly rate for all SA recipients in SA facilities.

> 1. The maintenance amount is the sum of the SA facility rate and the personal needs allowance.

> 3. For the SA Basic rate, if the a/b's TCMI is $1,466.51 or more, the a/b is not eligible for Special Assistance. 4. For the SA Enhanced rate, if the a/b's TCMI is $1,861.51 or more, the a/b is not eligible for Special Assistance.

> 3. The monthly SA payment amount is determined by deducting the TCMI from the Maintenance Amount. 4. When determining the SA payment amount, always round to the nearest dollar: reduce values $0.01 through $0.49 to the next lower whole dollar amount. Raise values $0.50 through $0.99 to the next higher whole dollar amount.

> If an individual's SA payment when rounded to the nearest lower whole dollar is $0.00, the individual is not eligible for Special Assistance.

> 1. The applicant's income for the month of entry is not counted if he/she enters the facility or meets all eligibility criteria after the first day of the month.

> e. Divide the monthly SA rate by the number of days in the month of entry to determine per diem rate (Round to the nearest hundredth). f. Multiply cost of care per diem times the number of days of care in the month to compute the cost of care. g. Add personal needs allowance ($70.00) to the adult care home rate h. Round amount to the nearest dollar for partial month payment.

IV.A requires that the applicant "meets all elements of eligibility".

**SAIH Manual SA-5300 IV, SA-5400 V** ([pp. 41-43](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/Special-Assistance-In-Home-Program-Manual-Rev-June-2026.pdf#page=41), 48):

> 3. For the SA Basic rate, if the a/b's TCMI is $1,466.51 or more, the a/b is not eligible for SAIH.

> 2. Subtract the a/b's TCMI from the applicable SA maintenance amount.

> Do not consider the applicant's income for a partial pay month.

> If a beneficiary is denied SSI due to spousal income but the beneficiary meets all other eligibility criteria for SAIH with countable income less than 100% of the federal poverty guideline, authorize the SAIH payment and calculate the payment amount using countable income.

## Required outputs

All Person, monthly.

| Output | PolicyEngine-US | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| Basic rate, enhanced rate (Money parameters) | `rate.basic`, `rate.enhanced`; `nc_sa_rate` | $1,397 and $1,792 from 2026-01-01 (SA-3220 II.A-B); $1,447 and $1,857 from 2027-01-01 (derived, see Interpretations). Each January 1 rate is the prior year's whole-dollar rate × (1 + SSA's announced COLA), rounded half-up to the dollar (108A-42.1; enhanced 2025: 1,700 × 1.025 = 1,742.50, so 1,743) |
| Personal needs allowance (Money parameter) | `personal_needs_allowance` | $70 (SA-3220 II.C) |
| Eligible (Judgment) | `nc_sa_eligible` | Approved setting (adult care home, special care unit, basic or enhanced in-home) AND (65 or over, OR 18-64 and disabled or blind, OR under 18 and blind in a facility) AND (receives SSI, OR is over income for SSI and meets SSI's other rules with own resources of $2,000 or less) AND not an inmate AND full-month payment ≥ $1 |
| TCMI (Money) | `nc_sa_countable_income` | Own income after the $20, $65 and one-half exclusions, plus SSI. A facility resident on an individual claim is budgeted at max(SSI, FBR − own countable income), except under V.D.1.e (1)-(3) |
| Full-month payment (Money) | `nc_sa_full_month_amount` | round-half-up(min(actual rate, published rate) + 70 − TCMI), floored at 0; eligible only if ≥ 1 (III.C) |
| Partial first month (Money) | `nc_sa` | round-half-up(round2(rate ÷ days in month) × eligible days + 70), with income not deducted and eligibility still required (IV.A; SA-5300 IV.C) |

## Companion tests

A-H come from the manuals' worked examples; I checked each figure against the manual text. I-K come from the statute with SSA's 2027 COLA, not from PolicyEngine output.

| Case | Inputs | Expected | Source | PolicyEngine-US case (`nc_sa.yaml`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Basic facility; maintenance 1,467; TCMI 995.47: 471.53 | 472 | SA-3220 III.B Example 1 (p. 207) | No PE case (nearest: "Case 1, basic facility with full SSI.", TCMI 994: 473) |
| B | Rate charged 1,000; maintenance 1,070; TCMI 997.47: 72.53 | 73 | III.B Example 4 (p. 208) | No PE case (nearest: "Case 12, lower contracted facility rate.", TCMI 994: 76) |
| C | Basic, entry October 5, 27 of 31 days: 45.06 × 27 + 70 = 1,286.62 | 1,287 | IV.B (p. 210) | "Case 22, first month twenty seven days ignores income." |
| D | Enhanced SCU, 27 of 31 days: 57.81 × 27 + 70 = 1,630.87 | 1,631 | IV.C (pp. 210-211) | No PE case |
| E | Basic, entry September 10, 21 of 30 days: 46.57 × 21 + 70 = 1,047.97 | 1,048 | VI.B Step 1 (pp. 217-218) | No PE case |
| F | SAIH basic: SSI recipient, TCMI 994 / non-SSI, TCMI 999.75 | 473 / 467 | SA-5300 IV.B (p. 42) | "Case 3, basic in home." (473); non-SSI: no PE case |
| G | SAIH basic, 20 of 31 days / enhanced, 14 of 31 days | 971 / 879 | SA-5300 IV.C Examples 1-2 (p. 43) | "Case 23, first month twenty days in home." / "Case 24, first month fourteen days enhanced in home." |
| H | Basic, TCMI 1,466.51 | Ineligible, 0 | SA-3220 II.E.3 (p. 207) | "Case 9, basic forty nine cents rounds down." (0); "Case 30, basic exact exclusive income limit prevents partial payment." (`nc_sa_eligible` false) |
| I | Basic rate, 2027: 1,397 × 1.036 = 1,447.29 | 1,447 | 108A-42.1(a); SSA 2027 COLA fact sheet | "Case 37, basic facility rate follows the cost-of-living adjustment in 2027." (`nc_sa_rate`) |
| J | Enhanced rate, 2027: 1,792 × 1.036 = 1,856.51 | 1,857 | 108A-42.1(b); SSA 2027 COLA fact sheet | `nc_sa_rate.yaml` "Case 8, enhanced special care unit rate follows the cost-of-living adjustment in 2027." |
| K | Adult care home, 2027, age 65, no income: 1,447 + 70 − 1,029 (2027 FBR) | 488 | 108A-42.1(a); SA-3220 II.C, III; SSA 2027 COLA fact sheet | "Case 37" (`nc_sa`) |

A probe on the PR branch reproduces A, B, D, E and F's non-SSI figure.

## Interpretations that change a result

- **COLA.** The "federally approved Social Security cost-of-living adjustment" in 108A-42.1 is SSA's announced percentage, rounded to a tenth (3.2%, 2.5%, 2.8% for 2024-2026; 3.6% for 2027), not the CPI-W ratio (3.62% for 2027, which gives a basic rate of $1,448). EFS-SA-CN-01-2026 p. 1 says the 2026 adjustment "is 2.8%". Chaining the rounded percentages from $1,285 and $1,647 reproduces every SA-3220 VIII chart rate for 2024-2026 (p. 219); chaining the CPI-W ratios gives enhanced rates of $1,742 and $1,790 for 2025 and 2026, not $1,743 and $1,792. The 2027 values are derived until NCDHHS publishes them. Pinned by `nc_sa.yaml` Case 37 and `nc_sa_rate.yaml` Case 8.
- **Income cutoff.** III.C is applied at the rate actually used: eligible only if round-half-up(rate + 70 − TCMI) ≥ 1. That gives II.E's $1,466.51 and $1,861.51 at the published rates and $1,069.51 at a $1,000 contracted rate (II.A). The test also applies in a prorated first month. Pinned by `nc_sa.yaml` Cases 29-32 and 35-36; in 2027 the basic cutoff is $1,516.51 (1,447 + 70 − 0.49), pinned by Cases 41-42.
- **One-third reduction.** A facility individual claim is budgeted at the FBR after the two-month window (V.B.1.b-c). Months 1-2 with reduced SSI are not modeled, so PE treats every facility month as ongoing. In-home budgets keep the reduction (V.D.1.e(3)). Pinned by `nc_sa_countable_income.yaml` Cases 3-4 and `integration.yaml` Cases 5-6.
- **Spouses living apart.** Spouses are separate claims from the month after they stop living together (20 CFR 416.1801(c)): with no income, $994 SSI each and $473 SA for the facility resident. PE needs separate marital units for this (`integration.yaml` Case 8). A couple sharing a room whom SSA treats as a couple keeps the couple amount (V.B.5.a, V.D.1.e(2); `nc_sa_countable_income.yaml` Case 5).
- **SSI application.** An applicant whose SSI countable income, deeming included, is below the FBR must receive SSI (SA-3100 I, II.A.6; 10A NCAC 71P .0603(3)); an SSI denial on resources also denies SA (SA-3110 V.K). An applicant over income, or one denied SSI for deemed spousal income (SA-5400 V), is paid without applying and is tested on own resources. Pinned by `nc_sa.yaml` Cases 26 and 38, `integration.yaml` Case 9 and `nc_sa_eligible.yaml` Case 9.
- **Blind children.** A legally blind child under 18 is eligible in a facility, which must be a specialized community residential center (SA-3100 II.A.1, III.C.3), but not in-home. Pinned by `nc_sa.yaml` Cases 16-17.

## Interpretations and gaps

- **Taking up SSI.** An applicant over the SSI income limit is paid without applying for SSI; one whose income would qualify must take it up (p.10, "if they might be eligible"). `ia_ssa.yaml` Cases 36-38; `ia_ssa_nonfinancial_eligible.yaml` Case 6.
- **Concurrent supplements.** The blind $22 is paid alongside residential care and IHHRC (6-B pp.20, 42; POMS F.1 code A; conflict 7), in Case 11 and integration Case 9, but not alongside SMME (p.76), in Case 24.
- **SMME couples.** Iowa Code 249.3(4)(g), 51.7(6) and p.77 don't address couples. An eligible couple's combined SSI income is compared with the two-person guideline (cases R-T). With a spouse who isn't aged, blind or disabled, the two-person guideline applies only when SSI deems that spouse's income; otherwise 8-E p.12 processes the applicant "as a one-person household" (case AV). Spouses that SSI computes separately, such as one in a medical facility, are each compared with the one-person guideline (case AT).
- **Poverty guideline year.** 441 IAC 75.1 revises the federal poverty level "annually on April 1", and Iowa's RC-0130 gives 120% as $1,565 / $2,115 until April 2026 and $1,596 / $2,164 from April. PolicyEngine-US uses the prior year's guideline before April (cases AR-AS), so the SMME boundary cases R-T run in April.
- **SMME and substantial gainful activity.** SGA doesn't preclude SMME disability (Iowa Code 249.3(4)(a)(2); 51.7(2); p.10). Federal SSI counts no income for a person it doesn't treat as disabled, so PolicyEngine-US applies SSI's income rules to that person's own income: the student earned income exclusion (416.1112(c)(3)), in-kind support and maintenance (416.1130, 416.1140) and the general and earned income exclusions. A spouse's income above $497 after child allocations is deemed as 8-E pp.12-13 do, and the result is compared with the two-person guideline; otherwise with the one-person guideline (cases AQ, AU, AY, AZ, BB-BD, BF and BG). A spouse SSI treats as aged, blind or disabled is not an ineligible spouse (8-E p.12), so the couple's income is combined with no $497 test (case BI), and nothing is deemed from a spouse in a medical treatment facility, who isn't a household member (416.1167; case BH). Income deemed from a parent and a spouse's intent to return from a facility are not modeled on this path.
- **IHHRC dependents.** The $497 allowance is SSI's ineligible child allocation, summed over the tax unit for a head or spouse recipient (cases U-V). Other dependents and unmet medical needs are an input.
- **Residential care couple in the entry month.** 6-B p.70 (Mr. W) budgets the couple and the dependent together. PolicyEngine-US splits a couple-budget month's care income and the couple rate equally between the spouses.
- **Residential care couples after entry.** SSA is assumed to pay each spouse as an individual from the month after entry (p.61), even a resident who doesn't take up SSI. PolicyEngine-US computes that amount because its federal SSI doesn't model spouses living apart. For the same reason, the spouse at home is still tested with the resident's resources after entry (cases AB-AG).
- **A spouse who enters later.** The sources don't settle a spouse who enters after the other spouse's month of entry. PolicyEngine-US gives that spouse the couple budget when either spouse received SSI, and deducts the SSI couple rate in that month.
- **Interest and dividends.** Excluded from care income and the family-life home $20 test (416.1124(c)(22)), while PolicyEngine-US federal SSI still counts them (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#10079), so SMME income and the SSA-paid amounts count them (case AI).
- **Impairment-related work expenses.** Entered at one-half for a resident without SSI, and not at all for an SSI recipient, whose SSI rises by the same amount (p.59; PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#3669; case AH).
- **Spouse identification.** SSI's spouse test, so a parent isn't paired with a claimed adult child when marital units are omitted (`ia_ssa.yaml` Case 65). Parental resources are still deemed to a child then (case AK).
- **2027.** The family-life home standard is the FBR plus $162: $1,191, with a couple amount of $818 (`integration.yaml` Case 10). The personal needs allowance follows the SSI COLA under Iowa Code 249.9A(1), $135, with nearest-dollar rounding inferred from General Letters 6-B-45 to 6-B-47 (case AP). The $38.47 is set through appropriations (249.12(3)) and the $518 has no published method, so both stay at their 2026 values.
- **Parental deeming.** Deemors include a co-resident stepparent ("in the same manner as SSI policy", p.46; 20 CFR 416.1202(b)(1)), in resources Case 6. With several eligible children, on which Iowa is silent, deemed income is divided equally. A parent receiving SSI isn't a deemor, but the two-parent allowance still applies. Parental resources are deemed only to a child that SSA deems to (p.9; case AM).
